target.title: feat(gateway): add ticketed read-only MCP App host
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

Closes #109851

## Summary

- Add a generic standalone MCP App host that exchanges a short-lived signed view ticket instead of exposing the operator Gateway bearer token.
- Keep the trusted shell on the Gateway origin and reuse the separate static sandbox listener; no view secret or dynamic app data enters the listener document.
- Keep the standalone host deliberately read-only and add one official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` fixture that drives both the existing authenticated Control UI host and the new standalone host over the real browser/transport path.

## What Problem This Solves

Future channel and standalone browser launches need to render one MCP App view without handing the page a reusable operator credential. The existing authenticated Control UI host is not a least-privilege launch boundary for an external browser surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process-local HMAC capability is bound to the current OpenClaw session key, MCP runtime session, view id, and view-lease deadline. The new HTTP boundary reconstructs only that live view, while the static host implements the stable MCP Apps initialization, ping, input/result, sizing, and teardown messages and rejects tool/resource requests.

This reuses the existing MCP runtime, view lease, sandbox proxy, and Gateway configuration. It adds no config/env surface, protocol version, channel launch UX, approval flow, or privileged capability.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, an authenticated Gateway client can obtain a standalone URL for the current view and open it without exposing the Gateway bearer token. Existing Control UI behavior is unchanged. There is no new default UI or channel action in this PR.

## Independent Landing and Backward Safety

- Existing `mcp.app.view` fields and semantics are preserved. `standaloneUrl` and its expiry are optional additions; ticket capacity, expiry races, or unexpected issuance failures omit those fields while returning the original successful view payload.
- The two new HTTP paths exist only behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Disabled installations and all other routes retain current behavior.
- The standalone URL is fully functional on this PR alone: initialize, ping, input/result delivery, read-only denials, reload, teardown, and rejection states require no later MCP Apps PR.
- The existing Control UI keeps its current app-only tool/resource authority. The conformance fixture proves shared/app-only tools and app resources remain available there while model-only tools remain denied.
- No current UI consumes the optional standalone field, and no current capability advertisement changes.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: the new route and optional Gateway response field are additive behind the existing MCP Apps gate. No launch button, channel integration, approval UI, tool/resource capability, or later-PR contract is advertised. A later PR may expose the already-working URL in channel UX, but is not required for any behavior enabled here.

## Evidence

- Real transport/browser path: an official self-contained `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.4` app ran through a real stdio MCP server, Gateway WebSocket authentication, Control UI Vite host, Gateway HTTP routes, static sandbox listener, and nested postMessage transports.
- Both hosts completed the stable `2026-01-26` initialize handshake and standard MCP `ping`, then received the original tool input and result.
- Control UI baseline: server tool/resource capabilities were advertised; the app-only companion tool and app resource succeeded; a model-only tool was denied.
- Standalone boundary: neither server tools nor server resources were advertised; tool and resource calls were denied; the only authorization header was `MCP-App v1...`, never `Bearer test`.
- Lifecycle: app-requested teardown removed the frame, reload reconstructed it, and a second load received the original result.
- Ticket security: unit/integration coverage rejects tampered, expired, wrong-session, wrong-runtime, wrong-view, replaced-view, and inappropriate reuse states; the browser scenario proves tampered and expired URLs fail.
- Origin/CSP review: the shell is static on the Gateway origin, the iframe is restricted to the exact separate sandbox origin, the listener stays static, the ticket remains in the URL fragment and is sent only in the dedicated authorization header, responses are no-store/no-referrer, and the shell never receives the Gateway token.
- Two final full-branch autoreviews after simplification/fixes reported no actionable findings. A reviewer-found missing standard `ping` response was fixed and exercised in both host modes before the clean final pass.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — full runtime and Control UI production build passed, including plugin SDK export and Control UI performance gates.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed with the frozen lockfile.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/e2e/mcp-app-conformance.e2e.test.ts` — 13 gateway assertions and the complete Chromium conformance scenario passed.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` — passed.
- Repeated canonical-base updates were rebased without conflicts; every final `git range-diff` showed all three commits patch-identical. The push used a fresh `upstream/main` fetch and verified ancestry immediately before publication.
- Blacksmith Testbox passed the build and broad static gates before exposing two strict fixture type errors that were fixed. Two later Testbox leases failed during delegated file sync before executing code, so trusted-source exact-head fallback proof ran in isolated temporary clones with frozen dependencies.

## Simplification and Scope

The PR is six files: three production files plus two focused Gateway tests and one maintained browser fixture. Net production growth is 463 LOC. Most of that is the single standalone module owning the capability store, HTTP/security boundary, static shell, and minimal protocol bridge; keeping those concerns together avoids a new public abstraction or duplicated policy. The remaining production additions are narrow route and optional-response wiring. No cleanup, config, launch UI, or privileged capability is mixed in.

## Known Gaps

- This does not add channel launch UX, approval UI, or standalone tool/resource authority.
- Tickets are intentionally process-local and expire no later than the view lease; a Gateway restart invalidates them.
- At the bounded live-ticket capacity, existing view responses continue to work but omit a standalone URL until capacity expires.
- Required GitHub CI on the published head remains the final landing gate.

target.title: feat: align native macOS chat with the web chat capability set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat lags the web Control UI chat in day-to-day capabilities, even though much of the machinery already exists. Several fully implemented shared surfaces were unreachable on macOS: the sessions manager sheet (`ChatSessionsSheet`) was dead code with no trigger anywhere, assistant reasoning/tool traces were hard-disabled, talk mode / voice notes / per-message Listen were implemented in `OpenClawChatUI` and wired on iOS but never injected by the macOS host, and the mac transport silently dropped the `verboseLevel` session setting. The composer also lacked three everyday web-chat features: input history recall, reply/quote, and per-session draft retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligning the native macOS chat with the web chat's capability set, preferring host wiring of existing shared code over new surface area. Two staged commits:

**1. `feat(macos)` — host wiring (mac app + minimal shared passthroughs)**
- Sessions manager reachable: **Sessions…** toolbar action + Shift-Cmd-S opens the Active/Archived manager (gateway search, rename, pin, archive, restore). The unreachable `showSessions` state in `OpenClawChatView` is deleted.
- Assistant reasoning & tool activity visible in the full window, with a persisted toggle (`openclaw.webchat.showAssistantTrace`, default on; compact panel stays minimal).
- New `MacChatSurface` observing wrapper bridges live state into the once-constructed `NSHostingController` hierarchy: talk control (bridged to the existing `TalkModeController`/`AppStateStore` paths without touching the menu-bar overlay), voice-note recording (blocked while Talk Mode owns mic capture), per-message **Listen** via gateway `tts.speak` bound to the transport's server lease with local synthesis fallback (mirrors the iOS client), and starter prompts on empty sessions.
- `MacGatewayChatTransport` now forwards `verboseLevel` in `sessions.patch` instead of dropping it.

**2. `feat(clients)` — shared composer parity (macOS + iOS)**
- Input history: Up/Down recall of prior inputs (session-scoped, cap 100, transcript-seeded plus locally sent slash commands, draft stash/restore, Escape cancels), mirroring `ui/src/pages/chat/input-history.ts` semantics. Slash-panel navigation keeps priority.
- Reply/quote: context-menu Reply → cancellable composer chip → outgoing message prepends the exact web blockquote format from `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` (`prependReplyQuote`, same Markdown escape set, 500/120 UTF-16 truncation limits), so transcripts look identical across surfaces.
- Per-session drafts: composer text survives session switches (in-memory; revision-guarded so races with in-flight sends cannot eat newer text). Accepted tradeoffs vs web (no cross-launch persistence, no attachment drafts) are noted in code comments.

All shared-package API changes are additive with defaulted parameters; iOS call sites compile unchanged.

## User Impact

macOS chat gains: full session management (rename/archive/restore/search), visible reasoning and tool activity with a toggle, talk mode + voice notes + read-aloud in the chat surfaces, starter prompts, `/verbose` that actually sticks, Up/Down input history, reply-with-quote, and drafts that survive session switching. iOS inherits the composer features. Docs updated: `docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md`.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawChatUI` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 48/48 XCTest; Swift Testing 853/856 with 3 pre-existing issues in untouched surfaces (see below)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --configuration release` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel` — 1280/1280 pass
- Gateway contracts verified in-repo: `tts.speak` (`src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts`), `sessions.patch` `verboseLevel` (`src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts:465`)
- Quote format verified against `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` `prependReplyQuote` + escape regex
- Pre-existing OpenClawKitTests failures (not touched by this PR, reproduced identically on two independent checkouts including one with composer-only changes and one with host-only changes): stale pairing-copy expectations (`GatewayErrorsTests.swift:59`, copy changed in 551c9637d8a3), watch legacy payload decode (`WatchCommandsTests.swift:74`, compat added in ec65e10df7fc and lost by a later watch commit), and a load-flaky attachment timeout (passes 9/10 isolated). CI does not run this suite; follow-up task filed to repair it and add coverage.

target.title: Bound ChatGPT websocket Blob frame reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT WebSocket responses accept string, ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView, and Blob-like frames. The Blob-like path previously called `arrayBuffer()` before checking any advertised frame size, so an oversized frame could force whole-frame materialization before the existing stream/body size caps had a chance to apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` now checks Blob-like `size` before calling `arrayBuffer()`. Frames larger than the existing ChatGPT Responses success-body cap fail with the existing WebSocket message-too-big close code instead of allocating the full body.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Blob-like WebSocket frame could be materialized in full even when it advertised a size above the provider's bounded response limit.

**After:** Oversized Blob-like WebSocket frames are rejected before `arrayBuffer()` is called. Normal string, ArrayBuffer, typed-array, and Blob-like frames within the cap keep the same decode behavior.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/audit-chatgpt-websocket-blob-bound` | Base: `upstream/main` (`c3f5526285859fced1f097cb1917b537e006c2f7`) | Head: `cccd1055aa9159bca1337c095efd0511c6af57a9`

### Regression tests

Added `rejects oversized ChatGPT websocket Blob frames before materializing them` in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`.

The test uses an explicit WebSocket transport mock that emits a Blob-like frame with `size = 16 * 1024 * 1024 + 1` and an `arrayBuffer` spy. It verifies the stream reports an error, does not fall back to SSE, and never calls `arrayBuffer()`.

### Commands run

```
$ gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "ChatGPT websocket Blob frames arrayBuffer" --limit 10 --json number,title,author,url
[]

$ gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "WebSocket message too big Blob frame" --limit 10 --json number,title,author,url
[]

$ git diff --no-index --check .codex-tmp\fresh-openai-chatgpt-responses.ts .codex-tmp\fresh-openai-chatgpt-responses.patched.ts
# passed

$ git diff --no-index --check .codex-tmp\fresh-openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts .codex-tmp\fresh-openai-chatgpt-responses.patched.test.ts
# passed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts -t "rejects oversized ChatGPT websocket Blob frames" --reporter=verbose
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'pathe' imported from D:\xwh_temp\openclaw\node_modules\vitest\dist\chunks\cac.D3xHeqeL.js
```

What was not tested: the local focused Vitest could not start because this checkout's local `node_modules` is missing Vitest's `pathe` dependency. The PR is draft until remote CI/Testbox or a repaired dependency install runs the focused test.

### Diff summary

```
packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts       | 14 +++++++++++++-
packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts  | 50 ++++++++++++++++++++++
```

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(transport): preserve HTTP status and Retry-After on Anthropic errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103849

On the default Anthropic Messages transport, a 429 response with a `Retry-After` header is turned into a plain `Error` with no status code or retry-after info. `AgentSession.prepareRetry` then falls back to fixed 2s/4s/8s exponential backoff regardless of the server's cooldown, causing all 3 retries to land inside the still-active rate-limit window.

## Fix

1. **Preserve**: parse `Retry-After` (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) and attach `status` + `retryAfterMs` to the thrown error in `createAnthropicMessagesClient`.
2. **Thread**: extract `retryAfterMs` onto the transport output and add optional field to `AssistantMessage`.
3. **Consume**: `prepareRetry` now uses `message.retryAfterMs` (clamped to 60s) via extracted `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` helper, falling back to exponential backoff when absent.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** (`anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` + `sdk.test.ts`):
- 136 total passed
- 3 new stub-server 429 tests: delta-seconds `Retry-After: 30`, HTTP-date format, no `Retry-After` header
- `prepareRetry` tests proving `delayMs === retryAfterMs` (30s honored) and clamp/fallback behavior

**Quality gates**:
- `oxlint` — exit 0
- `oxfmt --check` — exit 0  
- `tsgo:core` + `check:test-types` — exit 0

**Changed files**: 6 (`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`, `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`, `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`, `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-execution.ts`, + 2 test files)

target.title: fix(onboarding): stop recommending tools setup cannot activate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the no-AI onboarding state told users to install Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, or Grok Build and then "check again", even though guided setup cannot turn those installations into a verified inference route. Pi and OpenCode are explicitly classified as unavailable whole-agent/ACP routes, Gemini CLI is excluded from the tool-free setup probe, and Kimi/Grok CLI installs have no guided detection path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recommendation catalog introduced in #109681 is shared by CLI, macOS, and Control UI, so correcting its inclusion policy fixes every surface at the source. The catalog now contains only Ollama and LM Studio (`appGuidedDiscovery`) plus Claude Code and Codex CLI (native setup candidates); the removed tools remain supported through their existing provider, OAuth, or ACP-specific flows.

Changing the empty-state wording would still steer users into a non-working check-again loop, while adding a second runtime filter would duplicate the detector's capability policy.

## User Impact

Fresh setup users now see four install suggestions that can lead directly to a setup candidate OpenClaw can test and persist. This does not remove Pi, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, or xAI support; it only stops presenting their standalone CLI installs as fixes for the guided inference empty state.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Empty-state recommendations no longer include tool installs that guided setup cannot activate or verify.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, commit `f14d2ea27eff` on branch `fix/setup-recommend-usable-routes`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-recommended-installs.mts` - imports the production catalog loader, prints the returned IDs, and rejects any of the five unusable setup recommendations.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  PASS ids=ollama,lmstudio,claude-code,codex-cli unusable=none
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All clients receive only the four setup-compatible install cards from `recommendedInstalls`.
- **What was not tested:** The external installers and provider login flows were not executed because this patch changes only presentation catalog eligibility; existing dedicated support paths are untouched.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       110 passed (110)

$ OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- scripts/lib/recommended-tool-installs.json src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
EXIT=0

$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

The catalog regression failed before the JSON change by returning all nine IDs. `check:changed` first attempted its normal Blacksmith Testbox delegation; the host lacked the `blacksmith` executable, so trusted-source validation followed the documented local fallback and passed conflict, ratchet, dependency, format, boundary, typecheck, core lint, and script lint gates.

Structured Codex autoreview was attempted with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`, but the review transport returned HTTP 403 before a model response. The catalog producer, setup detector, all three client consumers, retained discovery contracts, removed tools' dedicated paths, and adjacent tests were reviewed manually.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - five misleading install cards are removed from the no-AI empty state.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config shape, persistence, default, or migration changes.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` with canonical agent, workspace-file, and package state
- bind `claws remove` consent to a dry-run `planIntegrity` digest and revalidate the complete plan before mutation
- reuse canonical agent deletion plus existing plugin and skill uninstall lifecycles
- remove only a final, unchanged, Claw-origin package that has not been adopted by a direct install
- retain independently owned, shared, pending, failed, modified, missing, or ambiguous artifacts and report why

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names resolve an install only when unambiguous; final agent ids always work and disambiguate repeated adds.

Remove is a two-step operation. The dry-run records the expected agent identity, managed-file digests, package ownership and canonical state, and root install state in `planIntegrity`. Mutation requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the plan, and fails closed if any consent-bearing input changed. Agent drift and unsafe workspace paths block the plan. Missing files are already removed, locally modified files are retained, and unchanged files are moved to nonce staging paths before final validation and deletion.

Package ownership is order-independent. Every Claw reference records whether the package originated from a Claw or existed independently. A later direct plugin or skill install adopts matching references as independently owned. Canonical install timestamps provide a conservative fallback if adoption state cannot be recorded. A final unchanged Claw-origin package is removed only after ownership is re-read immediately before execution, and deletion delegates to the existing plugin or skill uninstall lifecycle. Shared, adopted, drifted, incomplete, or uncertain packages are retained.

If package or file cleanup fails after the agent config commit, the root ledger remains partial and subordinate references stay available for status/doctor recovery. All commands remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and JSON contracts remain experimental.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package installation, ownership, and references
- This PR: lifecycle visibility and consent-bound, ownership-aware cleanup
- Next: #102306 portable export from the same provenance ledger

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`

`src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` invokes the real `src/entry.ts` CLI in an isolated state directory and passes the complete add -> status -> remove dry-run -> digest-bound consented remove flow. The final result is `openclaw.clawRemoveResult.v1` with `status: "complete"`; canonical agent config is removed and the managed workspace file is deleted.

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.
5. Confirm duplicate delivery does not cause concurrent duplicate dispatch.
6. Confirm the proactive reply targets the correct conversation/thread.

All logs and recordings must redact tenant IDs, user IDs, service URLs, tokens, credentials, IP addresses, and message content.

target.title: feat(feishu): handle opt-in VC meeting invites
target.body:
## Summary

- Register Feishu `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` in the bundled Feishu monitor.
- Keep VC invitations inert by default. `channels.feishu.vcAutoJoin: true` (or the account-level override) explicitly enables the join path.
- Convert enabled invitations into synthetic Feishu direct-message ingress from the inviter, reusing ordinary DM policy, pairing, allowlist, dynamic-agent, session, and reply-dispatch behavior.
- Route replies to the real inviter target (`user:<open_id>` / `user:<user_id>`), never to a synthetic meeting route.
- Ask the agent to join by validated nine-digit meeting number and pass `call_id` only when the installed join tool supports it.

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled Feishu channel did not register VC bot invitation events, so an invited OpenClaw bot could not receive the meeting context or start the join flow. Joining also changes the agent's live presence, so event subscription alone is not a sufficient safety gate. This PR adds the missing ingress while requiring an explicit, default-off `vcAutoJoin` opt-in.

## Linked context

Fixes #91677.
Supersedes #89751 with the same capability on the current Feishu ingress architecture.

## Evidence

The contributor tested live Feishu VC invitations against a local gateway and observed the Feishu event reach the bundled plugin, invoke the meeting join tool, join a live meeting, and preserve the inviter's ordinary Feishu DM route. The maintainer repair makes that existing join path opt-in; focused regression tests prove disabled invitations are ignored before dispatch and enabled invitations retain the proved behavior.

The supplied live observations and the focused test command below are the canonical behavior proof for this reviewed head.

The event still passes through the normal Feishu DM authorization boundary. Pairing-required and disallowed invitations do not reach the agent. Synthetic replies use the inviter's supported DM target and suppress replies to the nonexistent invitation message.

## Tests and validation

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/monitor.vc-meeting-invited-handler.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` — 4 files, 156 tests passed
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check`
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check`
- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check` — 719 files clean
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: yes, but default-off. No meeting join occurs unless `vcAutoJoin` is explicitly true.
- Configuration/operator action: enable `vcAutoJoin`, subscribe to `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1`, and grant `vc:meeting.bot.join:write`.
- Message delivery/session routing: invite-triggered turns use normal Feishu DM authorization and the real inviter target.
- Tool compatibility: `call_id` is optional in the generated instruction; the meeting number is the canonical join input.
- Security/privacy: no new credentials or persisted secrets; invite data is limited to join and reply-routing fields.
- Rollback: disable `vcAutoJoin`.

## Release note

Feishu: add opt-in VC meeting invitation auto-join through the normal authenticated DM ingress path. Thanks @zealous-dragon / @Ren1104.

target.title: fix(gateway): force-discard ACP runtime after cancel/close timeout
target.body:
Closes #106631

## What Problem This Solves

When `/reset` or session deletion hits a stuck ACP cancel/close operation, the bounded gateway cleanup can time out while the cached runtime and its per-session actor lane remain reusable. A later turn can then queue behind the poisoned operation or reuse the same broken runtime, forcing an operator to restart the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now calls a manager-owned `forceDiscardSession` path after cancel or close timeout. The manager:

- retires the old per-session actor generation so fresh work gets an independent queue tail;
- detaches the cached runtime immediately and best-effort closes it without awaiting another possible hang;
- fences late cache/meta mutations and late turn events from the retired generation;
- clears only the retired generation's active-turn bookkeeping, so it cannot erase a replacement turn.

Normal successful cancel → close behavior is unchanged. This adds no config, protocol, persisted-data, or CLI surface.

## User Impact

An ACP-backed session can recover through reset/delete timeout cleanup without restarting the gateway or allowing the discarded operation to affect the fresh runtime.

## Evidence

Exact tested head: `6d3a78a6fa28aa132536d570e3f05091764bdd4a`.

- [Fork-safe PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29576421602): success; 54 successful jobs, 0 failures, 0 pending.
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts`: 16/16 passed on Linux Node CI. Coverage includes stuck cancel and stuck close, a fresh turn completing while the retired operation remains unresolved, fresh handle reuse, stale completion rejection, and late-output suppression.
- `src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-acp-timeout.test.ts`: 2/2 passed on Linux Node CI in 507 ms. The tests drive the production 15-second timeout with a fake clock only after the hanging cancel/close operation has started; reset succeeds, force-discard runs, and fresh ACP metadata/session preparation follows.

target.title: feat(mac): Quick Chat v2 — enable toggle, agent switching, zoom entrance, window screenshots
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #109720 addressing review feedback on the Quick Chat bar: there was no way to disable the feature outside of unbinding the shortcut, the agent chip was a generic sparkles glyph, the "main session" capsule was noise, the entrance animation was a plain rise, and there was no way to send visual context.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Enable toggle:** Settings → General gains a "Quick Chat" switch (default on) that gates the global shortcut, hides the menu item, and disables the shortcut recorder. Turning it off dismisses an open bar.
- **Agent identity chip + switcher:** the sparkles glyph is gone. The chip renders the agent's avatar image (data-URI avatars from `agents.list`; remote http(s) avatar URLs are deliberately not fetched — a gateway-supplied URL must not become a blind request primitive against local networks — falling back to emoji, then a tinted monogram). With more than one agent configured the chip opens a native `NSMenu` listing agents; selection retargets the send using the canonical routing contract (`agent:<id>:<mainKey>`, or `sessionKey "global"` + `agentId` under global scope, per `validateChatSelectedAgent`). The "main session" capsule is removed; the placeholder ("Message <Agent>") carries the identity.
- **Fade+zoom presentation:** the bar now scales in from 96% with a fade (0.16s ease-out) and scales out on dismissal — the Voice Wake frame-animation pattern, no layer transforms.
- **Window screenshots:** a camera button starts a picker that overlays labeled cells on real windows (Peekaboo `WindowFiltering.isRenderable(.capture)` plus own-app/activation-policy exclusions, z-ordered hit testing, per-screen overlay panels). Clicking a window tears the overlays down first, captures via ScreenCaptureKit (`captureWindow(windowID:)`), transcodes through the shared `ChatImageProcessor` (1600px JPEG ≤3.5MB) off the main actor, and auto-sends as a `chat.send` attachment with the typed draft (or a default caption) — the whole pipeline held in the sending state and bound to an ownership token, presentation, and route so cancellations, agent switches, and re-presentations can never reroute or clobber a capture. First use without Screen Recording access shows an explicit grant alert; the strip's live polling picks up the grant.
- The capture-permission alert and strip continue to avoid `PermissionMonitor` (AppleScript probe).

Known limitation (accepted tradeoff, follow-up filed): after sending to a non-default agent under **global** session scope, ⌘Return opens the shared `global` session without an agent discriminator; threading `agentID` through the WebChat window contract is queued as its own change.

## User Impact

Quick Chat can now be fully disabled, shows who you're actually talking to (with fast agent switching), animates like a native quick-entry surface, and can send a window screenshot in two clicks. No new config surface beyond the toggle; no gateway changes; the only new TCC interaction is the user-initiated Screen Recording request.

Release-note context: `feat(mac): Quick Chat v2 — enable toggle, agent avatars and switching, fade+zoom entrance, click-a-window screenshots`.

## Evidence

- Review: eight structured autoreview passes (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh); 14 accepted findings fixed across the passes (route/presentation binding for the capture pipeline, pipeline ownership tokens, stale-permission-flow teardown, SSRF-by-avatar removal, draft-preservation during processing, bounded cancellable window discovery, GNOME-conflicting shortcut on the sibling branch, and more); two final findings consciously rejected with evidence in-thread (dismissal race is recovered by the existing transition-ID completion; global-scope navigation is the filed follow-up).
- Gates (local, Swift 6.4 toolchain): release build pass; `lint-swift` 0 violations; `format-swift` 0 changes; `git diff --check` clean. New/updated unit tests cover routing contract mapping, avatar parsing (incl. rejected remote URLs and oversized data URIs), pipeline token ownership (stale token no-ops), draft survival during an in-flight screenshot send, selection reset on refreshed agent lists, stale-routing lockout during refresh, toggle gating, placement scaling, picker filtering/hit-testing/label logic.
- `swift test` runs on the macos-swift CI lane (stable toolchain); the author machine's Xcode-beta cannot compile untouched `GatewayChannel*` test files (pre-existing).
- Locale artifacts refreshed for the new strings (inventory + 21 locales + regenerated Android strings).

Screenshots follow in a comment after the local install verification pass.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"
# Owner is "claude" — cross-agent confirmed ✓
```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓
- Before fix: label was written to `main_assistant` store → silently lost ✗

target.title: fix(telegram): bound polling stop cleanup with one shared concurrent barrier
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram polling shutdown previously ran its graceful-stop waits **serially per stop handle**: up to 2 × 15 s in `#runPollingCycle` (stopRunner, then stopBot) and another 15 s in the isolated-ingress cycle — while the polling lease could be released before grammY middleware had actually drained, letting a replacement account monitor start a competing poller (overlapping getUpdates → Telegram 409 conflicts).

## Why This Change Was Made

The three stop waits in `extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.ts` are replaced by **one shared, concurrent, time-bounded cleanup barrier** in `waitForGracefulStop`:

- Runner and bot shutdown are started **concurrently** (`Promise.allSettled`; both stop handles memoize their in-flight promise, so an abort-triggered stop is joined, not restarted).
- The barrier retains the polling lease until **both stop promises settle** or **one shared deadline** — the existing `POLL_STOP_GRACE_MS` (15 s) with the same `unref` semantics — expires. Worst-case cleanup drops from 2 × 15 s serial to a single 15 s window.
- The barrier is deliberately **not** shortened by the owner abort signal: abort still triggers the stops (`stopOnAbort` → `stopRunner()`, unchanged), but the cleanup wait itself is time-bounded only, so the lease is never released while grammY middleware is still draining (see Round 2 for the review that prescribed this design).
- Fast path preserved: already-settled stops resolve ahead of the deadline timer, so clean shutdown stays immediate.

No new config, no new env, no SDK or core changes.

## User Impact

- A replacement Telegram account monitor can no longer acquire the polling lease while the previous runner's stop is still pending — closing the overlapping-poller / 409 window on account replacement and watchdog restart.
- Shutdown latency is bounded by one shared 15 s deadline instead of up to 45 s of serial grace waits.

## Evidence

**Lease-handoff regression tests** (reviewer-requested):

- `holds the polling lease until a pending runner stop settles after abort` — abort fires with `runner.stop()` deferred; asserts the session does NOT return while the stop is pending (lease cannot be handed to a replacement poller), then settles and asserts completion; also asserts the barrier started `bot.stop()` concurrently.
- `releases the polling lease at the grace deadline when the runner stop never settles` — fake-timers: a never-settling stop holds the lease until exactly the deadline, which then forces completion.
- **Control-red proof**: both tests FAIL against the pre-redesign head (abortable grace resolved instantly → lease released early: `expected true to be false`); they pass on this head.

**Checks:**

- `polling-session.test.ts` — 80/80 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` / `tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0; oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean

---

<details>
<summary>Round 1 (2026-07-16): original abortable grace-window approach — superseded after review</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

`waitForGracefulStop` in `extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.ts:56` races the in-flight `stop()` against a bare `setTimeout(resolve, POLL_STOP_GRACE_MS)` (15 s) that never receives the session's `AbortSignal`. All three call sites run from polling-cycle `finally` blocks where `this.opts.abortSignal` is in scope (`polling-session.ts:705`, `:893`, `:894`), but the signal was never threaded through.

When the gateway stops a Telegram account — or a watchdog restart is already draining — the abort fires first and the runner/bot stop is initiated by `stopOnAbort`. If that stop is slow or wedged, the teardown path still rides out the full 15 s grace window **per call**, sequentially: up to 30 s in `#runPollingCycle` (stopRunner + stopBot) and another 15 s in the isolated-ingress cycle, all after shutdown was already requested. An abort that arrives mid-grace during a watchdog restart is likewise ignored until the window elapses.

Sibling waits around it already honor the signal: `#waitBeforeRestart` sleeps via `sleepWithAbort(delayMs, this.opts.abortSignal)` (`polling-session.ts:204`), and `waitForSpooledHandlerTaskSettlement` resolves early on abort. Only the graceful-stop window was unwired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grace window is now `sleepWithAbort(POLL_STOP_GRACE_MS, abortSignal, { ref: false })`, wrapped so its abort rejection settles the race early instead of throwing through the shutdown path — the same shape merged in #108561 (Discord READY retry backoff) and consistent with #108408 (Feishu retry loop). `{ ref: false }` preserves the old timer's `unref` semantics, so a pending grace timer never keeps the process alive. `stop()` rejections still propagate exactly as before; only the abort rejection is swallowed.

`abortSignal` is an optional parameter, so any other caller keeps the previous timer-only behavior. The three polling call sites now pass `this.opts.abortSignal`. `waitForGracefulStop` is exposed via a `testing` export re-exported from `test-api.ts` so the regression test drives the production function directly, mirroring #108561.

No new config, no new env, no SDK or core changes; the only signature change is the optional parameter.

## User Impact

- Stopping or restarting a Telegram account no longer stalls up to 15 s per graceful-stop wait after abort was requested; the wait ends on the abort event (measured: ~1 ms response, see Evidence).
- Watchdog restarts that race a shutdown abort now tear down immediately instead of finishing the grace window first.
- Happy path is unchanged: a stop that settles before the window still wins the race, and the 15 s ceiling still bounds a wedged stop while the session is alive.

## Evidence

### Before fix (this branch, `waitForGracefulStop` body reverted to `origin/main` — control-red)

Uncommitted `scratchpad/telegram-graceful-stop-abort-proof.mts` drives the production `waitForGracefulStop` with a wedged `stop()` (never settles), a real `AbortController`, and wall-clock timers:

```
[201ms] >>> abort fires
[15002ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (mid-grace abort)
[15001ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (pre-aborted signal)
[151ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (stop settled at 150ms, no abort)
```

Abort fired 201 ms into the 15 000 ms window; the wait still rode out the full window — 14.8 s wasted per call. A pre-aborted signal (the normal shutdown case) also waited the full 15 s.

### After fix (this branch)

Same harness, same timing:

```
[247ms] >>> abort fires
[249ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (mid-grace abort)
[0ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (pre-aborted signal)
[152ms] waitForGracefulStop resolved (stop settled at 150ms, no abort)
```

The abort listener now interrupts the grace sleep immediately (~1 ms response), a pre-aborted signal returns instantly, and a stop that settles at 150 ms with no abort still wins the race unchanged.

### Mutation proof

Reverting only the `waitForGracefulStop` body to the `origin/main` version (keeping tests and the `testing` export) makes exactly the two new abort tests fail — `resolves early when the abort signal fires mid-grace` (15 122 ms) and `does not ride out the grace window when the signal is already aborted` (15 009 ms) — while the two non-abort tests keep passing. Restoring the fix turns the full file green again.

### Regression tests

New `describe("waitForGracefulStop")` block in `polling-session.test.ts` runs the production function with a real `AbortController` and real wall-clock timers (the file-level `sleepWithAbort` mock is locally restored to the real implementation via `vi.importActual`): mid-grace abort resolves in ~100 ms instead of 15 s, pre-aborted signal resolves immediately, stop-settles-first still wins, and omitting the signal keeps the old behavior. Two pre-existing tests that counted `sleepWithAbort` calls now filter to the 2-arg backoff calls, since the grace window legitimately adds 3-arg `{ ref: false }` calls.

### Tests & checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts` — 79/79 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the three changed files — 0 errors
- `git diff --check` — clean

Prod-only non-test change: one function body, three call sites, one test-only export (+1 re-export). Follows the merged precedents #108561 and #108408; sibling to open #109604 (Telegram startup-probe abort — disjoint files).

AI-assisted; reviewed before submission.


---

</details>

---

## Round 2 (2026-07-17)

**Review addressed:** Codex P1 — "patch is incorrect". Passing `this.opts.abortSignal` into the graceful-stop waits made the wait resolve immediately on the normal account-stop path (owner signal already aborted), so `runUntilAbort()` returned while grammY `runner.stop()` was still draining middleware → the monitor released the polling lease → a replacement account monitor could start a competing poller → overlapping getUpdates → Telegram 409 conflicts.

**Redesign (as prescribed by the reviewer):** the abortable per-stop grace sleeps are replaced by ONE shared, non-abortable, bounded cleanup barrier in `waitForGracefulStop`:

- Abort/restart still TRIGGER the stops (`stopOnAbort` → `stopRunner()`, unchanged); the grace wait itself is now time-bounded only and never resolves early on the owner abort signal.
- The barrier starts runner and bot shutdown concurrently (`Promise.allSettled(stops.map(stop => stop()))`; both stop handles memoize their in-flight promise, so abort-triggered stops are joined, not restarted) and races that against a single fixed deadline — the existing `POLL_STOP_GRACE_MS` (15 s) constant with the same `unref` semantics. Worst-case cleanup drops from 2 × 15 s serial to one shared 15 s window.
- Fast path preserved: already-settled stops resolve through the microtask queue ahead of the deadline timer, so clean shutdown stays immediate (covered by a fake-timers test that needs zero timer advance).
- The isolated-ingress cycle uses the same barrier for its single `stopBot`.

**Regression coverage (reviewer-requested lease-handoff tests):**

- `holds the polling lease until a pending runner stop settles after abort` — abort fires with `runner.stop()` deferred; asserts `runUntilAbort()` does NOT return while the stop is pending (i.e. the monitor cannot hand the lease to a replacement poller), then settles the stop and asserts completion; also asserts the barrier started `bot.stop()` concurrently.
- `releases the polling lease at the grace deadline when the runner stop never settles` — fake-timers run: a never-settling `runner.stop()` holds the lease until exactly the grace deadline, which then forces completion.
- Control-red proof: both tests FAIL against the previous round's code (abortable grace resolved instantly → lease released early: `expected true to be false`); they pass on this round. The unit-level `describe("waitForGracefulStop")` block was rewritten to the new contract (concurrent start, pending-stop hold, deadline force-complete, settled fast path); the previous pre-aborted/mid-grace abort tests were removed because the barrier no longer takes a signal — abort-triggers-stop is covered at the session level, and mid-grace abort now provably does NOT shorten cleanup (the whole point of the finding). The two `sleepWithAbort` call-count assertions reverted to their upstream form since the barrier no longer sleeps via `sleepWithAbort`.

**Checks (round 2):**

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts` — 80/80 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0; `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `oxlint` on the three changed files — clean; `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat floating composer for the Tauri companion
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Linux/Tauri companion has no quick way to message the agent — every interaction goes through the full dashboard. This is the cross-platform sibling of the macOS Quick Chat bar (#109720): a summonable floating composer that fires a message at the default agent's main session and gets out of the way.

## Why This Change Was Made

First deliberately minimal step, matching the shell's existing architecture (CLI delegation, static frontend, on-demand windows):

- **Window:** frameless, transparent, always-on-top `quickchat` webview created on demand (same pattern as the Canvas window), centered on the cursor's monitor with its top edge at ~22% of the work area, excluded from window-state restoration. CSS-driven fade+zoom in/out (140ms/100ms) with a JS↔Rust hide handshake; hides on Escape, focus loss, close-request, successful send, or toggle.
- **Entry points:** `Ctrl+Shift+Space` global shortcut on X11 (Alt+Space is GNOME's window-menu grab and can never be registered; the existing X11-only gate applies — the plugin's Linux backend doesn't support Wayland) and a **Quick Chat** tray item that works everywhere including Wayland. The existing `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+O` dashboard shortcut is untouched; the handler now dispatches by shortcut identity.
- **Send path:** a window-scoped `quickchat_send` command runs `openclaw agent --message-file <owner-only tmp> --session-key main --json` detached — the message is staged in a 0600 file and deleted after the turn because argv is world-readable through procfs and an agent turn can run for minutes. The bar shows the accepted state immediately; a failed turn surfaces as a desktop notification with the first stderr line. `Ctrl+Enter` additionally opens the dashboard.
- **Identity chip:** `quickchat_identity` resolves the default agent from `openclaw agents list --json` (60s cache) and renders emoji or a hue-hashed monogram with a "Message <Agent>" placeholder.
- **Security posture:** all five commands verify the calling window label; the new capability is scoped to the `quickchat` window with its own permission set; no permission strip on Linux (no TCC equivalent), and no accessibility/window-capture features in this first step by design.

## User Impact

Linux companion users get a keyboard-first composer for the main session. Replies stay in the normal session (dashboard). No changes to existing windows, shortcuts, or gateway behavior.

target.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

## Summary

- Complete the existing Control UI MCP App host bridge with safe, text-only `ui/message` support routed through the normal visible chat-send path.
- Advertise messaging only for fresh, authorized app views; reconstructed views remain explicitly read-only.
- Propagate live theme and iframe dimensions through the official MCP Apps host-context bridge without remounting, with observer/listener cleanup on teardown.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI could render MCP App resources and service app tool/resource requests, but an app could not safely ask the user to send plain text through the host chat, and mounted apps did not receive live theme or size changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the already-present iframe/resource reconstruction architecture. It reuses the existing widget-prompt validation and `WIDGET_PROMPT_EVENT` send seam, adds host-owned exact-text confirmation for MCP App requests, and uses the official `AppBridge.setHostContext` lifecycle. It does not add a second send route, config/env surface, protocol version, or privileged approval path.

The implementation adds a small explicit `readOnly` lease marker because a fresh app may legitimately have zero app-callable tools, while a transcript-reconstructed preview must remain resource-only. Tool-count inference could not represent both states safely.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, a visible and focused fresh app can request that the user send one plain-text message. The host shows the exact text for confirmation, then sends through the existing chat composer path. Hidden/background frames, empty or oversized text, slash commands, and rate-limit excesses are rejected. Apps also receive current theme and dimensions as they change.

## Independent landing and backward safety

- The gateway response field is additive. Older Control UIs ignore it; a newer UI talking to an older gateway sees the field absent and installs/advertises no message handler.
- Existing widget prompts use the same extracted validation/send helper without the MCP App confirmation callback; their existing behavior is covered by the widget-prompt and tool-card regression suites.
- App tool/resource handlers, app-only policy, sandbox origins, inner opaque iframe isolation, routes, config, and protocol versions are unchanged.
- Fresh views with an explicit authority set may advertise messaging even when that set is empty. Legacy views without authority and reconstructed `readOnly` views fail closed.
- No behavior enabled by this PR requires a later MCP Apps PR.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: all behavior remains behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Within that gate, `message.text` is advertised only when a fresh view has explicit current-run authority and the host handler is installed. Reconstructed views can still render/read resources but cannot message or call tools. Rich or multi-block `ui/message` content is intentionally unsupported.

## Evidence

- Genuine browser flow: a browser-bundled `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` ran through the real Control UI Vite app, dedicated sandbox HTTP server, and nested iframe bridge. The official initialize handshake advertised `message.text`; exact host consent was required; accepted text produced the normal `chat.send` request (`deliver: false`); the app received its response; live light-theme and container-dimension changes propagated without remounting.
- Focused exact-head proof: 89/89 assertions passed across MCP view leases, transcript reconstruction, gateway authorization, text/focus/visibility/size/rate/slash boundaries, existing widget prompts, host-context updates, and cleanup.
- Production build passed, including the Control UI lazy chunk (`mcp-app-view-registration`, 63.26 kB) and Control UI performance limits.
- Changed-surface checks passed through formatting, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and related policy gates. An earlier Plugin SDK baseline mismatch was independently reproduced on untouched canonical main; the current canonical base includes its unrelated generated/declaration repairs.
- A first CI run exposed a production lint suppression for the SDK's request-style `onmessage` setter. The handler now registers through that documented public setter via a typed wrapper, without a suppression or private schema import; the component and suppression-ratchet tests pass, followed by two clean fresh autoreviews.
- Two fresh autoreviews after the final safety fixes reported no actionable findings (confidence 0.98 and 0.94). Canonical-base updates preserved the exact nine-file product diff.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.node.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.widget-prompts.test.ts`
- Exact-head `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm build`
- Fresh `$autoreview` passes before and after simplification/final safety edits

## Simplification and scope

The PR changes five production files and four focused test files. Net production growth is +60 LOC: the message handler/host-context lifecycle and explicit read-only authority marker are offset by deleting the duplicated widget-prompt policy/send implementation. No additional abstraction module, route, config, or compatibility shim was added.

## Known gaps

- This does not enable MCP Apps globally or implement later rollout work.
- Only one plain text content block is accepted; rich content remains rejected.
- Transcript-reconstructed previews intentionally remain read-only until a fresh run grants current authority.

target.title: fix(ui): derive live cron and skill counts for Simple Automations card
target.body:
## Summary

The Quick Settings Automation card hardcoded cronJobCount and skillCount to 0, always displaying misleading zero counts regardless of real Gateway state. skillCount is now derived from config (same pattern as existing mcpServerCount), and cronJobCount is fetched once via gateway cron.status RPC on entry.

- Problem: Control UI Settings → Simple → Automations always showed "0 scheduled tasks" and "0 skills installed" even when the Gateway had real Cron jobs and Skills installed, because both values were hardcoded to 0.
- Solution: skillCount reads from config.skills.entries (config-driven, no RPC), cronJobCount fetches once via cron.status RPC when entering quick settings mode, with null-to-zero fallback until data arrives.
- What changed: `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` (+40/-3): added skillCount() helper, added cronJobCount state with one-shot loadCronStatus() RPC loader, wired counts into renderQuickConfig(). `ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts` (+37/0): added tests for non-zero counts and singular label rendering.
- What did NOT change: MCP server count (remains config-derived via mcpServerCount), polling behavior (no periodic cron.status calls), i18n keys, UI layout, channels/security/appearance quick settings.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #107852
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Operators opening Control UI → Settings → Simple → Automations always saw "0 scheduled tasks / 0 skills installed" regardless of real Gateway state, because cronJobCount and skillCount were hardcoded to 0 in renderQuickConfig(). This made healthy Cron and Skills installations look unconfigured and sent users to troubleshooting pages unnecessarily. The MCP server count already worked correctly by deriving from config — the same pattern should apply to the other two counters.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Control UI Simple Automations card hardcodes cron and skill counts to zero instead of deriving real values. Issue #107852.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (NewStartOS V4.4.2), Node v22.22.3, vitest jsdom environment, branch `fix/quick-automation-counters-107852`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts --run

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /media/vdc/githubode/openclaw-fixskills

 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts (37 tests) 2761ms
   ✓ renders the single-column settings sections with stable target ids
   ✓ changes the Control UI language from General settings
   ✓ drills into model settings from the Model row
   ✓ shows channel status and connect actions
   ✓ renders automation counts from props
   ✓ renders singular automation labels for count of 1
   ✓ renders Gateway host identity and resources
   ... (30 more tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
   Start at  11:25:16
   Duration  5.09s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.96s
```

```console
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 21ms on 2 files with 212 rules using 8 threads.
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Automation card renders "3 scheduled tasks / 5 skills installed / 2 MCP servers" when counts are non-zero (unit test verified).
2. Automation card renders "1 scheduled task / 1 skill installed / 1 MCP server" for singular counts (unit test verified).
3. skillCount is derived from config.skills.entries keys, following the same pattern as mcpServerCount.
4. cronJobCount is fetched once via cron.status RPC when quick settings mode is entered, with null-to-zero fallback until response arrives.
5. Counts reset to null on page/mode change and gateway reconnect, allowing retry on next entry.

**What was not tested**: A live Gateway + browser session showing the populated Automation card with real Cron and Skills data. The cron.status RPC path is unit-tested through the rendered output, but end-to-end verification against a running Gateway was not performed in this environment.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

In `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts:848-850`, the `renderQuickConfig()` method constructs the automation card state with literal zero values:

```typescript
automation: {
  cronJobCount: 0,
  skillCount: 0,
  mcpServerCount: mcpServerCount(configObject),
}
```

The MCP count works because `mcpServerCount` derives from `config.mcp.servers`. The Cron and Skills counts were never wired to any real data source.

Provenance: `carried forward by` commit 65e1232 (Control UI architecture refactor). The hardcoded zeros were introduced as placeholder values in the new Config-page layout.

Confidence: `clear`.

## Regression Test Plan

N/A — the fix is additive only. Existing tests continue to pass. New tests cover the previously uncovered behavior (non-zero counts rendering, singular labels). No config/API/shape changes.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

The Simple Automations card now displays the actual number of scheduled Cron tasks (from cron.status RPC) and installed Skills (from config.skills.entries) instead of always showing 0. On initial load before the RPC completes, the Cron count shows 0 briefly until the response arrives; the Skills count is immediately correct from config.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No (cron.status is an existing read-only Gateway RPC)
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Non-zero automation counts render correctly (3 scheduled tasks, 5 skills installed, 2 MCP servers); singular labels render correctly (1 scheduled task, 1 skill installed, 1 MCP server); skillCount() helper handles missing/malformed config gracefully; cronJobCount null state renders as 0; all 37 existing tests continue to pass.
- Edge cases checked: null/missing skills.entries config (returns 0), null cron.status response (falls back to 0), gateway disconnect before RPC completes (request id guard discards stale response).
- What you did NOT verify: Live Gateway + browser end-to-end flow; cron.status method-scope failure behavior (handled by null-to-zero fallback).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix follows the existing mcpServerCount pattern for skillCount (config-driven, synchronous, zero-RPC) and adds a minimal one-shot cron.status RPC for cronJobCount (no polling, no additional infrastructure).
- **Refactor needed**: No. The approach is minimal and does not introduce new abstractions.
- **Alternative considered**: Loading both inventories via skills.status + cron.list RPCs with polling — rejected because it adds unnecessary Gateway load, requires i18n changes for loading/unavailable states, and substantially increases the diff size (competing PR #108681 has +402 lines across 66 files). The skill count is statically available in config and does not need an RPC.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: The cronJobCount one-shot load fails silently on transient Gateway RPC errors, keeping the counter at 0 until the user navigates away and back. This is a known limitation.

**Mitigation**: The null default provides a 0 fallback (same as the current hardcoded behavior, so no regression). Retry occurs automatically on page/mode change (settings mode toggle, navigation to another tab and back, Gateway reconnect). The risk of permanent "stuck at 0" is low because most Gateway connections are stable, and the skillCount (config-driven) always works immediately.

**Compatibility impact**: None. No config, API, or migration changes. Existing behavior is preserved: MCP count unchanged, all quick settings layouts and i18n keys unchanged.
