target.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

New users finish onboarding with a bare install even when their Mac is full of apps
OpenClaw already has plugins and skills for (Notion, Obsidian, Slack, 1Password,
Things, …). Nothing connects "what is installed on this machine" with "what OpenClaw
can do with it", so discovery is manual catalog browsing.

# Why This Change Was Made

Adds installed-app plugin/skill recommendations to `openclaw onboard`:

1. **Scan** — enumerate `/Applications`, `~/Applications`, and a small allowlist of
   `/System/Applications` (TCC-free: no permission dialog can fire — `readdir`,
   Launch Services, and Spotlight metadata are unprotected paths; verified on a real
   machine).
2. **Candidates** — loose name matches from the official plugin/channel/provider
   catalogs plus top-3 ClawHub skill search hits per app (concurrency 4, 5s/request,
   20s overall budget; failures degrade to catalog-only candidates).
3. **AI matching** — one completion on the model route the wizard just verified. The
   model receives app names + candidate descriptions and returns genuine matches with
   a tier (`recommended`/`optional`) and a short reason. No curated bundle-id map to
   maintain; the model rejects coincidental name overlaps (naive matching paired
   Linear→`line`, Zed→`zededa`, Parallels→`parallel` in prototyping — the live test
   asserts these traps stay dead).
4. **Consent surface** — the wizard step is deliberately "magical" (product decision):
   no consent prompt before the scan, but the scanning progress line and the results
   note both disclose that app names are matched using the configured model and
   ClawHub search, and `wizard.appRecommendations: false` disables the feature
   entirely. The results step lists detected apps and installs only what the user
   selects (recommended tier pre-checked, explicit skip).
5. **Remote gateway path** — the TS node-host gains the `device.apps` invoke command
   Android already ships (same envelope; macOS emits `label`/`bundleId` where Android
   emits `label`/`packageName`). Node-side sharing is **off by default** (privacy
   parity with Android's consent toggle) via node-host config /
   `--share-installed-apps`; disabled invokes return the typed
   `INSTALLED_APPS_SHARING_DISABLED` error. The gateway allowlists the command for
   macOS nodes and strips it everywhere when the kill switch is off. Local onboarding
   scans directly and does not use the node command.

Also fixes a latent bug this feature exposed: `runSetupInferenceTest` applied the
32-token verification-probe output cap (`SETUP_INFERENCE_TEST_MAX_TOKENS`) to every
completion, so any custom prompt longer than a few words returned a reasoning-only
turn and "Agent couldn't generate a response." Custom-prompt completions now use the
model's own output budget; the probe keeps its cap.

Prior art: Setapp is the only mainstream product doing install-scan → recommendation;
its trust framing (scan silently, show the detected list, act opt-in) is what this
follows, with explicit disclosure because app names do leave the machine.

# User Impact

- `openclaw onboard` (non-quickstart, macOS, working model route) gains one optional
  step: detected apps → tiered multiselect → install. Zero matches or any failure
  (offline ClawHub, model error, malformed model output) skips the step silently;
  onboarding never blocks on this feature.
- New config key `wizard.appRecommendations` (default enabled) to disable.
- Mac/headless nodes can opt in to sharing their app inventory with the gateway
  (`--share-installed-apps`, persisted in node-host config, default off).

# Evidence

- **Live end-to-end test** (real ClawHub `/api/v1/search` + real OpenAI
  `gpt-5.6-luna`): `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENAI_API_KEY=… pnpm test:live
  src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.live.test.ts` — **passed** (76s). Fixture
  inventory of 9 real apps incl. traps; model matched Notion→`notion`,
  Obsidian→`obsidian`, Slack→`slack-api`, Linear→`linear`, Things→`things-mac`,
  1Password→`1password` and produced none of the trap pairings.
- **Unit tests** (all passing): scanner fixtures/filtering/sorting + Linux-safe plist
  reader injection; candidate dedupe + ClawHub failure degradation; matcher zod
  filtering incl. fenced-JSON/extra-key/overlong-reason tolerance; node `device.apps`
  gating + Android-parity envelope; gateway allowlist + kill-switch stripping;
  node-host config persistence; wizard gating/pre-check/skip/install paths
  (`pnpm test src/infra/installed-apps.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/node-host/invoke-device-apps.test.ts src/node-host/runtime.test.ts
  src/node-host/config.test.ts src/wizard/setup.app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts src/wizard/setup.test.ts
  src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts`).
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `git diff --check` —
  all green.
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): two accepted findings fixed (Linux CI
  plutil dependency in the scanner test; unbounded ClawHub phase → 20s budget). The
  remaining consent-first finding is consciously rejected as the documented product
  decision (default-on with disclosure + kill switch); an inline comment records it.
- Real-machine scan prototype: 45/52 apps matched, no TCC prompt, <2s.

target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumePendingForBatchScan` in `src/skills/workshop/history-scan.ts` built session cursors by calling `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` without filtering out `NaN`. When a session's `updatedAt` is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `updatedAtMs` became `NaN`, which then propagated through the resume cursor into subsequent scan iterations.

The downstream comparison `cursor.updatedAtMs > lastReviewedAtMs` returns `false` when `updatedAtMs` is `NaN`, so affected sessions were silently skipped on resume instead of being re-scanned from the correct point.

## Fix

Filter `sessionCursors` so any entry whose `updatedAtMs` is not a finite number is dropped before it can reach the resume cursor. This preserves existing behavior for valid timestamps while ensuring malformed ones cannot poison the resume state.

Export `toStoredState` as a named export (instead of wrapping it in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag it as unused.

## Evidence

- **Local test run** (3 regression tests pass):
  ```
  RUN  v4.1.9
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  3 passed | 23 skipped (26)
  ```
- **New tests cover**: session with unparseable `updatedAt` excluded from cursors; valid timestamps preserved.
- **No production behavior change**: valid timestamps continue to produce cursors exactly as before; only `NaN` entries are now filtered out.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers
target.body:
Related: #109724 (Codex-parity slice 1: this PR is the provider-neutral question RPC that PR deliberately deferred)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents had no first-class way to ask the human a structured question and wait for the answer. The embedded agent could only guess or write prose questions into chat; Codex harness questions got a text-only prompt on channels; and there was no provider-neutral pause/prompt/resume primitive that web UI and message channels could share (the pattern Claude Code ships as `AskUserQuestion` and Codex ships as `request_user_input`).

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the provider-neutral question runtime deferred by #109724, modeled on the existing exec-approval subsystem (the established blocking pause→prompt→resume template):

- **Gateway question runtime**: transient in-memory `question.request` / `question.waitAnswer` / `question.resolve` / `question.get` / `question.list` RPCs plus `question.requested` / `question.resolved` broadcasts under a new `operator.questions` scope (additive; no protocol version bump). Answers are validated against the stored record (unknown ids, cardinality, option membership) and canonicalized before terminalizing; `isSecret` and duplicate option labels are rejected at the request boundary.
- **`ask_user` tool** for the embedded agent (main sessions only, not subagents): 1–3 questions, 2–4 options each (labels ≤64 chars), `multiSelect`, free-text "Other" always available, recommended-option-first convention, `timeoutSeconds` 30–3600 (default 900). The tool blocks like exec approvals; expiry returns a `no_answer` result telling the model to proceed with best judgment.
- **Chat delivery**: the question is delivered to the originating conversation while the tool blocks — as a `MessagePresentation` with native tap-to-answer buttons via a new runtime-authored `{type:"question"}` presentation action (Telegram inline keyboards `tgq1:` ≤64 bytes, Discord custom ids `ocq` ≤100 chars, Slack Block Kit `slq1:`), degrading to numbered text on button-less channels. A plain text reply (number, label, or free text) answers on any channel; the reply is consumed as the answer instead of steering into the run.
- **Control UI**: one unified in-thread question card serving both gateway `ask_user` questions (broadcast-driven, click/multi-select/free-text, resolve over the gateway, terminal states incl. answered-elsewhere/expired) and the existing Codex stream questions from #109724 (composer submit path unchanged).

Codex upstream contract checked directly at `openai/codex@9ff47868eb`: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/request_user_input.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1585-1637` (schema conventions: header ≤12 chars, recommended-first, forced free-text "Other", root-thread-only — mirrored here). Converging the Codex/Copilot harness bridges onto this runtime is a named follow-up, not part of this PR.

## User Impact

Agents can now pause and ask a real question with buttons. Users answer by clicking in the web Control UI, tapping a native button on Telegram/Discord/Slack, or just replying in text on any channel; the agent resumes with structured answers. Docs: `docs/tools/ask-user.md`.

Pending card (web):
![pending](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/01-question-pending.png)
Answered:
![answered](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/02-question-answered.png)
MultiSelect:
![multiselect](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/03-question-multiselect.png)
Terminal states (answered elsewhere / expired):
![terminal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/04-question-terminal-states.png)

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end proof** on a source-checkout gateway (isolated `--dev` state dir, `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`): agent called `ask_user` with a single-select + multiSelect pair, blocked 1m03s, the web card rendered in-thread, options were clicked (Staging + Integration/E2E), the gateway resolved, and the agent resumed enumerating exactly those answers. This live run also caught and fixed a gating bug (`isEmbeddedMode()` is the TUI-host flag, not the embedded-runner flag — `ask_user` was invisible to normal gateway runs until commit `ce0251e6bb9`'s fix).
- **Playwright e2e** `ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts` (3 tests, mock gateway): render → resolve payload shape (`{answers:{deploy_target:{answers:["Staging (Recommended)"]}}}`) → resolved state; multiSelect arrays; answered-elsewhere + expired terminal states. Screenshots above are its artifacts.
- **Focused suites** (local, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`): gateway question manager + RPC handlers + protocol validators, ask_user tool (normalize/execute/claim/abort races), subscriber delivery, outbound presentation precedence, per-channel envelope round-trips incl. byte limits, UI prompt state machine + card + thread placement — all green (500+ tests across the touched files).
- **Typecheck/lint**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, targeted oxlint — green (Testbox + local fallback when Testbox returned 429).
- **Build**: full `pnpm build` green, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`.
- **Autoreview** (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): three iterations; 7 findings accepted and fixed (answer validation at resolve, isSecret fail-closed, duplicate-label rejection, UI retry latch, reconnect `QUESTION_NOT_FOUND` terminalization, option-label bound, answer canonicalization); final run clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope): converge Codex/Copilot harness user-input bridges onto the question runtime; reaction-based answering on WhatsApp/Signal/iMessage; unbind channel buttons after resolution; MCP elicitation routing (pending the 2026-07-28 MRTR spec).

target.title: improve: let Code Mode use declared tool result shapes
target.body:
Related: #109288
Follow-up to #109651 and #109290

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode learned exact tool ids and compact input signatures from #109651, but every tool result still appeared as unknown. Even when a tool had a stable structured result, models often spent one exec returning the raw value and another exec processing fields they could have known up front. This left avoidable model turns, tokens, and latency in common multi-operation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted OpenClaw core and plugin tools can now declare an optional `outputSchema` for `AgentToolResult.details`. Code Mode and Tool Search expose a bounded TypeScript-style output hint only when that schema is complete and closed; open, oversized, unsupported, MCP, and client schemas remain unknown and raw-first.

OpenClaw compiles trusted output schemas before execution, then validates final details after normal hooks. Framework-owned pre-execution policy blocks remain outside the success schema and are recognized by object identity, so calls reject with the denial reason before generated code can treat a block as a successful value; tool-authored blocked lookalikes still fail validation. Runtime/provider normalization preserves the result contract when it clones tool definitions. The compact renderer has strict depth/property/character/union bounds and normalizes AJV-style nullable schemas so every validator-accepted `null` remains visible to generated code. Remote and client schemas stay deferred as `input: "unknown"` and use object identity for catalog reuse, preventing attacker-sized metadata walks while preserving schema-replacement invalidation. `agents_list` adopts the contract as the first built-in example.

The change also promotes Code Mode to a dedicated `/tools/code-mode` documentation page with Quickstart, runtime semantics, guest API, output-contract authoring, trust/validation rules, fallback behavior, debugging, and validation guidance. The old `/reference/code-mode` route redirects to it.

## Maintainer Decision

Approve `outputSchema` as the supported optional plugin API for describing and validating `AgentToolResult.details` across Code Mode and Tool Search. Tools that omit it retain existing behavior. Opted-in tools get pre-execution schema compilation, final-details validation, and framework-owned policy-result preservation.

## User Impact

Code Mode can call and process tools with declared result shapes in the first exec instead of paying a raw-inspection round trip. Unknown outputs keep the safe existing raw-first behavior. Plugin authors get one documented result contract shared by Tool Search and Code Mode, without trusting remote MCP or client schema claims.

## Evidence

Live multi-provider matrix: four validated Code Mode tasks per provider over the real Agent runtime and a 72-tool catalog with adversarial decoys. Baseline is merged #109651; after is this branch.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Validated tasks | 11/12 | 12/12 | +1 |
| Model turns | 29 | 26 | -10% |
| Code Mode exec calls | 17 | 14 | -18% |
| Decoy calls | 0 | 0 | unchanged |
| Total latency | 81.4s | 70.4s | -13% |
| Input tokens | 38,827 | 36,025 | -7% |
| Output tokens | 2,388 | 2,380 | unchanged |

Stress: three complete Code Mode matrices produced 34/36 validated tasks, 78 turns, 42 exec calls, 57 underlying service calls, and zero decoy calls. Anthropic and Google were 12/12; OpenAI was 10/12. Both misses were the model filtering singular fixture value `plum` with the plural word `plums` after selecting the correct real tool, not a discovery, transport, schema, or decoy failure. A final OpenAI/Google pass kept every completed task at two turns and one exec. The final Anthropic retry hit provider overload before tokens or tools; earlier Anthropic stress was 12/12.

Validation:

- Exact final head: 272 focused tests passed across the live-bench parser, Code Mode, Tool Search, runtime normalization, schema hints, `agents_list`, plugin SDK, descriptor cache, and optional tool metadata.
- Blacksmith Testbox on the earlier pre-review head: 254 focused tests passed; all changed gates passed, including core/plugin/test/script typechecks, full lint, SDK API/surface/boundary checks, and the full production build. Later contract fixes passed their exact-head focused suites locally and receive fresh hosted CI before merge.
- Adversarial regressions cover malformed schemas before side effects, post-hook result validation, policy-block rejection with preserved reason, blocked-lookalike rejection, nullable scalar/object contracts, cloned runtime tools retaining hints and validation, schema replacement, closed/truncated/unsupported shapes, huge keys/catalogs, untrusted client/MCP schema deferral, and zero traversal of hostile schema proxies.
- Source-blind behavior contract: satisfied at 0.86 confidence; all seven clauses passed, including state-changing irrigation, missing-tool recovery, zero decoys, provider-error classification, and docs navigation/redirect behavior.
- Autoreview: clean on the runtime-normalization fix at 0.97 confidence, policy-block contract fix at 0.95, and nullable-contract fix at 0.94. Earlier review-driven fixes added pre-execution compilation, explicit completeness tracking, unsupported-shape rejection, bounded untrusted metadata handling, and the documented `input: "unknown"` sentinel.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core inspects that declaration before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. A yield result from a default/parallel tool is rejected before the runtime control handler is invoked.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration; only tools that opt into yield must declare sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.
- Require yielding tools to declare `executionMode: "sequential"` and reject incompatible results.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json

    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },

    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"

    },

```

### Finalization and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Agent-core tests prove a non-sequential yielding tool is rejected before its control handler runs.
- Agent-core tests prove a sequential yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Catalog-path coverage proves Tool Search / Code Mode preserves plugin result control.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

target.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy
target.body:
Related: #54565

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot currently decide whether rich inbound WhatsApp messages should bypass debounce or choose a debounce window for a specific account, DM, group, conversation, or sender. Doing either requires changing product defaults or adding more core configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed `inbound_debounce` plugin hook. The hook receives the channel's default action, duration, a read-only debounce key, conversation context, and media/location/quote facts. It may explicitly debounce, bypass, or select a duration.

WhatsApp now consults this hook while preserving its current defaults. Control commands still dispatch immediately. Rich batches preserve all media and structured context, and split safely when multiple quotes or locations cannot be represented without data loss.

This is an API-based alternative to the product-level approaches in #103049 and #100970. It lets plugins provide those policies without adding native product settings.

AI-assisted with Codex.

## User Impact

There is no behavior change when no plugin implements the hook. Plugins can opt media, locations, or quoted replies into batching and can choose different windows for DMs, groups, accounts, conversations, senders, or their own policy scopes.

The hook is bounded by a two-second timeout, preserves per-conversation arrival order, keeps control commands immediate, and cannot replace the debounce key to merge unrelated conversations.

target.title: fix(ui): show cross-agent child sessions in the sidebar on request
target.body:
Fixes #95295.

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Control UI sidebar session discovery across configured agent scopes.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The default sidebar request is intentionally scoped to the selected agent, and the sidebar projection independently removes subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. The prior opt-in implementation widened both layers through shared session state, so a later scoped chat refresh could replace the all-agent rows while the **All agents** button remained pressed.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Persisted child-spawned work could exist in another agent store but remain undiscoverable from the sidebar, and the previous toggle could visibly claim an all-agent view while showing only one agent's sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause repair.
- **Complete shipped solution:** The default sidebar remains scoped. Pressing **All agents** performs the existing unscoped `sessions.list({})` request into sidebar-owned state, enables child/spawned rows only for that local result, and leaves shared canonical scoped state untouched. Canonical list revisions and session-created events coalesce background refreshes of the local result; stale responses, disconnects, gateway-client replacement, and session-capability replacement cannot reactivate old rows.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The sidebar now owns both sides of the opt-in invariant: its unscoped data source and its child-row projection. A scoped refresh can continue publishing canonical state without contradicting the pressed control, and disabling the control immediately returns to the latest canonical scoped result.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The existing `sessions.list` contract and combined session-store loader remain authoritative. Omitting `agentId` is already the canonical all-agent read; this patch does not add a protocol, schema, config, persistence, or migration contract.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** The Sessions page, command palette, primary-session selection, chat picker, default scoped visibility, gateway protocol/schema, persisted transcript format, and session migration behavior are unchanged.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** The behavior is default-off and sidebar-only. Maintainers should still confirm that opt-in sidebar discovery of persisted child transcripts across configured agents is the intended product boundary.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state`, visibility boundary, compatibility, and performance.
- **Risk explanation:** The opt-in mode can reveal persisted child/subagent transcripts from other configured agent scopes and performs a bounded all-agent list read. It does not mutate shared canonical state or stored sessions.
- **Why acceptable:** The wider visibility is explicit and user initiated; archived, global, unknown, and cron rows remain excluded; the existing list limit/configured-agent behavior remains in force; and default behavior is unchanged.
- **Patch quality notes:** Production changes are confined to sidebar state/rendering, the existing navigation projection, and the scope-control style. The additional E2E change is the requested visible-browser regression. No suppression directives, skipped tests, lockfile changes, protocol changes, or unrelated refactors were added.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for contributor-side correctness and the current-main port; final cross-agent transcript visibility scope remains an explicit maintainer product decision.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Enable **All agents** in the sidebar and rediscover an existing cross-agent child-spawned session, while newly created sessions and canonical list revisions refresh that opt-in view.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** With the control off, the sidebar remains agent-scoped and continues hiding subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. Scoped chat/session refreshes continue publishing their normal canonical result.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** The proof uses an isolated local Gateway and deterministic persisted session stores rather than real user transcripts or an external provider conversation. It exercises the real Gateway session-store loader, WebSocket request/response path, built Control UI, and Chromium rendering at the exact submitted head.

## Evidence

### Current-head real Control UI proof

The inspectable live proof was captured at pre-sync commit `e7d3636cccbdb2352a083f8ed9fa40fe697941ed` with an isolated Gateway started from this worktree and Chromium connected to `127.0.0.1:19001`. The current-main port preserves the same submitted behavior and was revalidated through the full browser-level session-management E2E; the live bundle is retained as prior-head evidence rather than represented as an exact-current-head capture.

| Default scoped sidebar | After pressing **All agents** |
|---|---|
| ![Scoped sidebar shows only the main session](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mikasa0818/1fd7cae0025fec937603e90d4d852f12/raw/e7d3636c-control-ui-sidebar-scoped-2026-07-11.svg) | ![All agents sidebar shows same-agent and cross-agent spawned children](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mikasa0818/1fd7cae0025fec937603e90d4d852f12/raw/e7d3636c-control-ui-sidebar-all-agents-2026-07-11.svg) |

- **Inspectable proof bundle:** [screenshots, exact command log, Gateway/WebSocket log, and captured `sessions.list` frames](https://gist.github.com/mikasa0818/1fd7cae0025fec937603e90d4d852f12).
- **Scoped observation:** The initial real `sessions.list` request included `agentId: "main"`; the response came from the main-agent store with 2 rows, and the cross-agent child had DOM count 0.
- **All-agents observation:** Pressing the control sent a real `sessions.list` request without `agentId`; the response path was `(multiple)` with 3 rows and included `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child` with `spawnedBy: agent:microservice-log-query:main`; the row had DOM count 1.
- **Verdict:** Default scope hides the cross-agent spawned child; the explicit default-off **All agents** mode reveals it without replacing shared scoped session state.

### Automated validation

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash; Node `v22.17.0` for repository checks (non-fatal warning against the preferred `>=22.19.0` floor); Node `v24.18.0` for the live Gateway/browser proof; pnpm `11.2.2`; repository Playwright Chromium; current `origin/main`.

The current-main integration also keeps categories discovered only in the all-agent result available to drag/reorder and move-to-group controls instead of binding those controls to the scoped canonical result.

RF-002 — disclosed as the explicit default-off visibility boundary and existing sidebar-action exposure. RF-003 — fixed with captured real combined-store `sessions.list` response and rendered DOM proof. ## What Problem This Solves

`createAcpClient()` spawns an agent child process but never attaches an error listener. If the agent binary is missing or fails to start, the unhandled `'error'` event on the ChildProcess can crash the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawned agent already has an `agent.on("exit", ...)` handler in `runAcpClientInteractive`, but no corresponding error listener. An error listener prevents unhandled-error crashes when the agent process fails to start (ENOENT, permission denied, etc.).

## Evidence

All 57 ACP client tests pass, no regressions:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  57 passed (57)
```

## Merge Risk

Low — single-file, +4 lines. The error listener logs via the existing `log` function (verbose-only) and lets the existing `client.initialize()` failure path handle the dead agent naturally.

target.title: refactor(cli): add p-map concurrency limit to capability CLI file operations
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. On large batches (100+ files), this causes simultaneous file reads, image conversions, downloads, and inference requests at once - risking EMFILE exhaustion, OOM from buffering many image buffers simultaneously, connection-pool starvation for provider API calls, and CPU overcommit from parallel sharp image processing.

**Solution**: Replace 5 `Promise.all(x.map(async ...))` calls with `pMap(x, ..., { concurrency: 20 })`. p-map v7.0.5 is already a direct dependency used across 7+ other modules in the codebase including media-understanding, cron, and gateway server startup. No new dependencies introduced.

**What changed**: 5 async mapping locations in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`. Each function's core logic and error handling remain unchanged - only the outer iteration over the dynamic array is bounded. The inner `Promise.all` calls within each iteration (e.g., per-image metadata gathering) continue to run in parallel as a fixed-size batch within one pMap slot.

**What did NOT change**: Inner per-item `Promise.all` calls, error handling, return types, function signatures, behavior for single or small-batch invocations. Zero behavioral change at the small scale covered by existing unit tests.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
`capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. On large batches (100+ files), this causes simultaneous file reads, image conversions, downloads, and inference requests at once - risking EMFILE exhaustion, OOM from buffering many image buffers simultaneously, connection-pool starvation for provider API calls, and CPU overcommit from parallel sharp image processing.

**Root Cause**:
`capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core inspects that declaration before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. A yield result from a default/parallel tool is rejected before the runtime control handler is invoked.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration; only tools that opt into yield must declare sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.
- Require yielding tools to declare `executionMode: "sequential"` and reject incompatible results.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json

    "loaded": true,

    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"

    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },

    },
```

- Agent-core tests prove a non-sequential yielding tool is rejected before its control handler runs.

target.title: Bound QA runtime parity mock request reads

## What Problem This Solves

QA runtime-parity reads `${mockBaseUrl}/debug/requests` from a local mock server and previously used `response.json()` directly. That endpoint should return a small request snapshot array, but a broken mock server could return a large successful body and make the QA process buffer it before any validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the unbounded `response.json()` call with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper using a 256 KiB cap and a 30s idle timeout. The existing fail-closed behavior is preserved: non-OK, malformed, oversized, or stalled mock responses are caught by `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` and treated as missing mock tool-call data.

target.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider-boundary correctness for Anthropic and Mistral plus shared retry/overflow hardening:

- Anthropic streams crashed with a TypeError when a proxy omitted `usage` from `message_delta` events.
- One-hour prompt-cache writes were billed internally at the five-minute rate (1.25x input) even though the API charges 2x — cost reporting under-counted whenever long cache retention was active. Usage now carries the 1h bucket separately and prices it correctly, keeping the aggregate `cacheWrite` field intact.
- Anthropic-compatible backends that emit and accept empty thinking signatures lost their thinking blocks on replay; an opt-in `allowEmptySignature` compat flag preserves them (default unchanged).
- Mistral prompt caching was never engaged or accounted: requests now send the prompt-cache key and cached-token usage is parsed into `usage.cacheRead`.
- The Anthropic SDK's hidden default retries (2) stacked under the app's own retry policy; the client now defaults to 0 when unset.
- Retry classification missed HTTP 524 (Cloudflare origin timeout), abrupt socket-close failures, and camel-case `ResourceExhausted` — all transient, all previously fatal.
- Context-overflow classification missed parenthesized token-count messages ("maximum context length (262144)") and "maximum allowed input length" phrasings — those errors skipped compaction recovery and stuck sessions.
- Simple-stream requests with a max-token budget near a full context drew provider validation 400s that the overflow classifier cannot recognize; output budgets are now clamped against a conservative input estimate so requests survive and real overflows stay classifiable.

## Why This Change Was Made

These are correctness gaps users hit as crashed streams, silently wrong cost numbers, stuck sessions after context overflow, and hung retries. The classifiers stay purely classificatory; policy remains with the caller.

## User Impact

Anthropic streams tolerate lean proxies; cost reporting is accurate under 1h cache retention; Mistral costs drop via real prompt caching; transient CF/socket/gRPC failures retry instead of failing hard; overflow recovery triggers reliably; near-full-context requests degrade gracefully instead of erroring.

## Evidence

- 163 focused unit tests across 7 files (usage buckets, cost math, compat replay, clamp math, table-driven retry/overflow classifiers).
- **Live verification (real API keys)**: `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.live.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.live.test.ts` — 4/4 passing: Anthropic stream with usage, 1h cache-retention request parsing `cache_creation` buckets with correct cost accounting, thinking-signature survival, and a Mistral stream with cache-field parsing.
- Full changed-file gate green on hosted runner (baselines, three typecheck lanes, lint, boundaries): run 29563721450.
- Plugin-SDK API baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow for the additive `Usage.cacheWrite1h` / `allowEmptySignature` contracts; `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` green post-rebase.


**Additional live probes (real API keys):** overflow classification proven against providers' *current* error strings — a deliberately context-exceeding request to Anthropic and to OpenAI Responses each classify as overflow via `isContextOverflow` (guarding compaction recovery against provider error-string drift), and the new output-clamp path completes successfully on a near-full context instead of a validation 400. Anthropic+Mistral 6/6, OpenAI Responses 4/4 keyed runs.

## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

target.title: fix(codex): continue after optional input timeout
target.body:
Related: #109724

AI-assisted: Codex was used to implement and review this change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex through the app-server integration could see an optional input question keep the turn waiting for a human answer or a broader run timeout, even when Codex supplied an automatic-resolution window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The user-input bridge now preserves the optional app-server deadline, returns an empty answer set when that exact window expires, and clears the timer through the existing request cleanup path after a human answer, abort, replacement request, or server-side resolution.

The implementation follows the current upstream Codex contract at `openai/codex@315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304`: [`autoResolutionMs` is the optional client auto-resolution window](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L71-L77), [Codex bounds it before dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L123-L133), and [app-server forwards the value to its client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L703-L746). [The TUI's fixed countdown is an explicitly client-specific policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/request_user_input/mod.rs#L281-L300), so OpenClaw honors the app-server wire value instead of copying that policy.

The branch also updates the Codex binding test fixture for the `features.goals: false` entry introduced by #109724. This is a test-only baseline correction; it does not change runtime configuration.

## User Impact

Optional Codex questions can now release the waiting turn automatically at the requested deadline. Human answers still win when submitted in time, and completed or replaced requests leave no stale timer that can affect a later question.

## Evidence

- Real Codex app-server 0.144.1 behavior proof over stdio, using the production client and bridge with a real 60-second clock (no mocked transport or fake timers):

```json
{"phase":"initialized","serverVersion":"0.144.1","transport":"stdio"}
{"phase":"completed","requestCount":1,"observedAutoResolutionMs":60000,"requestElapsedMs":60006,"emptyAnswers":true,"requestedEventCount":1,"resolvedEventCount":1,"protocolResolvedCount":1,"blockReplyCount":1,"turnCompleted":true,"continuationTokenSeen":true,"passed":true}
```

- The live run proves the optional request returned an empty answer after its wire deadline, emitted exactly one requested/resolved lifecycle pair and one protocol resolution, then the same turn continued to its expected assistant marker.
- Node 24.15 focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/user-input-bridge.test.ts` - 1 file and 16 tests passed.
- Node 24.15 binding proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` - 1 file and 63 tests passed.
- Fake-timer coverage verifies exact expiry, human-answer cleanup with no second settlement, abort cleanup, and replacement-request timer isolation.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for all three changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review found no accepted or actionable findings after checking callers, cleanup races, the binding fixture, and the upstream protocol contract.

## Summary

The Quick Settings Automation card hardcoded cronJobCount and skillCount to 0, always displaying misleading zero counts regardless of real Gateway state. skillCount is now derived from config (same pattern as existing mcpServerCount), and cronJobCount is fetched once via gateway cron.status RPC on entry.

- Problem: Control UI Settings → Simple → Automations always showed "0 scheduled tasks" and "0 skills installed" even when the Gateway had real Cron jobs and Skills installed, because both values were hardcoded to 0.
- Solution: skillCount reads from config.skills.entries (config-driven, no RPC), cronJobCount fetches once via cron.status RPC when entering quick settings mode, with null-to-zero fallback until data arrives.
- What changed: `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` (+40/-3): added skillCount() helper, added cronJobCount state with one-shot loadCronStatus() RPC loader, wired counts into renderQuickConfig(). `ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts` (+37/0): added tests for non-zero counts and singular label rendering.
- What did NOT change: MCP server count (remains config-derived via mcpServerCount), polling behavior (no periodic cron.status calls), i18n keys, UI layout, channels/security/appearance quick settings.

## Change Type (select all)

## Motivation

Operators opening Control UI → Settings → Simple → Automations always saw "0 scheduled tasks / 0 skills installed" regardless of real Gateway state, because cronJobCount and skillCount were hardcoded to 0 in renderQuickConfig(). This made healthy Cron and Skills installations look unconfigured and sent users to troubleshooting pages unnecessarily. The MCP server count already worked correctly by deriving from config — the same pattern should apply to the other two counters.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Control UI Simple Automations card hardcodes cron and skill counts to zero instead of deriving real values. Issue #107852.

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No (cron.status is an existing read-only Gateway RPC)
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

- Verified scenarios: Non-zero automation counts render correctly (3 scheduled tasks, 5 skills installed, 2 MCP servers); singular labels render correctly (1 scheduled task, 1 skill installed, 1 MCP server); skillCount() helper handles missing/malformed config gracefully; cronJobCount null state renders as 0; all 37 existing tests continue to pass.
- Edge cases checked: null/missing skills.entries config (returns 0), null cron.status response (falls back to 0), gateway disconnect before RPC completes (request id guard discards stale response).
- What you did NOT verify: Live Gateway + browser end-to-end flow; cron.status method-scope failure behavior (handled by null-to-zero fallback).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix follows the existing mcpServerCount pattern for skillCount (config-driven, synchronous, zero-RPC) and adds a minimal one-shot cron.status RPC for cronJobCount (no polling, no additional infrastructure).
- **Refactor needed**: No. The approach is minimal and does not introduce new abstractions.
- **Alternative considered**: Loading both inventories via skills.status + cron.list RPCs with polling — rejected because it adds unnecessary Gateway load, requires i18n changes for loading/unavailable states, and substantially increases the diff size (competing PR #108681 has +402 lines across 66 files). The skill count is statically available in config and does not need an RPC.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: The cronJobCount one-shot load fails silently on transient Gateway RPC errors, keeping the counter at 0 until the user navigates away and back. This is a known limitation.

**Mitigation**: The null default provides a 0 fallback (same as the current hardcoded behavior, so no regression). Retry occurs automatically on page/mode change (settings mode toggle, navigation to another tab and back, Gateway reconnect). The risk of permanent "stuck at 0" is low because most Gateway connections are stable, and the skillCount (config-driven) always works immediately.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users could not configure an all-uppercase NSEC private key or send to an all-uppercase NPUB target. Bech32 permits an encoding to be entirely lowercase or entirely uppercase, but OpenClaw rejected the uppercase form before `nostr-tools` could decode it.

The Nostr key boundary now recognizes both canonical lowercase prefixes and valid all-uppercase prefixes, then continues to delegate checksum and mixed-case validation to `nostr-tools`. The lightweight setup entry and target shape detector follow the same rule; mixed-case Bech32 remains rejected.

Users can paste uppercase NSEC/NPUB values, including values copied from uppercase QR representations, into Nostr setup and DM targets without converting them to lowercase first.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

merge-risk: low

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two catalog rollback guards compared timestamps returned by `Date.parse` without checking for `NaN`:

1. `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts`
2. `isMonotonicRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-snapshot-store.ts`

Both used `Date.parse(candidate.generatedAt) < Date.parse(current.generatedAt)`. When either `generatedAt` string is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `Date.parse` returns `NaN`, and `NaN < NaN` evaluates to `false`. The rollback guards therefore reported "not a rollback" and accepted a candidate that should have been rejected, allowing the catalog snapshot store to move backward to an older or malformed snapshot.

## Fix

Mirror the same defensive policy in both guards:
- If the **candidate's** `generatedAt` is invalid (`NaN`), conservatively treat it as a rollback so malformed candidates cannot downgrade the store.
- If the **current** snapshot's `generatedAt` is invalid, treat the candidate as newer (not a rollback) so a broken current state can still be repaired.

target.title: Guard Skill Workshop update applies against delta drafts
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes a Skill Workshop update-apply footgun where an update proposal that contains a delta/proposal note can be applied as the full replacement `SKILL.md`.

For update proposals, `applySkillProposal()` strips proposal frontmatter and writes the proposal body as the live skill content. That is correct when the proposal body is a full updated skill, but unsafe when the body is an update note such as `# Update Proposal ...` with "proposed changes" instructions. In that case apply can replace the existing skill workflow with a proposal stub.

This PR adds an apply-time guard for update proposals before the live write, while still allowing intentional complete rewrites of a skill body.

## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop `action=update` proposals are meant to carry a complete replacement `SKILL.md`. Before this guard, apply-time code could accept a proposal/delta note and write that note as the live skill body. That risks destroying the actual skill procedure.

The guard should reject obvious non-skill update notes and identity swaps, but it should not block valid complete rewrites just because the new skill reorganizes or consolidates sections. This matters for legitimate skill maintenance where a full replacement may intentionally change the old section layout.

## What changed

- Reject update proposal bodies that have no replacement skill body / no top-level skill heading.
- Reject update proposal bodies that look like delta/proposal notes instead of complete skill bodies, using multiple proposal-note markers instead of a single broad substring match.
- Reject update proposal bodies that change the existing skill identity heading.
- Allow complete replacement `SKILL.md` bodies that intentionally reorganize or consolidate old `##` sections.
- Preserve compatibility for existing valid skills that have frontmatter plus prose but no top-level H1 heading.
- Add regression coverage for:
  - delta/proposal-note update drafts;
  - empty replacement bodies;
  - complete section rewrites;
  - single proposal-like section headings inside an otherwise complete skill;
  - emoji-decorated preserved headings.

## Duplicate/adjacent work check

- #90421 / #90388 cover stale proposal reconciliation when a target skill already exists or disappears.
- #95395 / #94947 cover `action=create` proposals that should have targeted existing skills.

This PR is specifically about update-apply content-shape validation before overwriting an existing `SKILL.md`.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): stop oversized streaming TTS audio
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ElevenLabs streaming TTS could continue delivering provider
audio beyond the 16 MiB limit already enforced by the buffered path. An
oversized or unbounded response could therefore keep consuming network and
Discord playback resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ElevenLabs stream owner now enforces the shared `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` policy
without buffering. It owns the provider-body reader, waits for upstream
cancellation before surfacing an overflow, and releases the reader lock on
normal completion, read failure, overflow, consumer cancellation, and early
public release. The release hook composes reader cleanup with transport cleanup
and remains safe to call more than once.

Provider configuration, request/response types, output formats, and other
speech providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

Normal ElevenLabs voice replies continue streaming into playback unchanged.
Oversized responses now fail at a deterministic 16 MiB boundary, close the
provider response, stop Discord playback, and complete transport cleanup.

## Evidence

### Actual OpenClaw streaming consumer

A guarded local ElevenLabs-compatible HTTP fixture exercised the production
provider and Discord consumer chain on the rebased head:

```text
buildElevenLabsSpeechProvider().streamSynthesize
  -> fetchWithSsrFGuard
  -> Readable.fromWeb
  -> createDiscordOpusPlaybackStream
```

Observed after the final diff:

```text
normal: completed=true, opus_packets=15, playback_ended=true, release_settled=true
overflow: error="ElevenLabs API error: audio response exceeds 16777216 bytes"
overflow: provider_connection_closed_before_release=true
overflow: node_input_destroyed=true, playback_destroyed=true
overflow: ffmpeg_stopped=true, release_settled=true
```

The normal response used generated valid MP3 audio. The overflow response used
a valid oversized ID3 metadata prefix so the byte boundary was reached without
an external service. Credentials, loopback endpoint details, and local paths
are omitted; no live ElevenLabs key or external Discord account was used.

### Regression and extension coverage

- Before the lifecycle repair, the overflow regression observed the upstream
  provider stream still locked after cancellation (`expected false`, received
  `true`).
- Before the release-hook repair, both early-release regressions observed zero
  upstream cancellations and a still-locked provider stream.
- Complete ElevenLabs TTS file on the final candidate: 15/15 tests passed,
  including unread and partially consumed early-release cleanup.
- ElevenLabs plugin lane on the final candidate: 5 files and 36/36 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed on the submitted files.
- The max-lines ratchet passed on the exact current-main merge preview with
  1,184 grandfathered suppressions.

target.title: feat(write): add capability-gated native append
target.body:
## Summary

Adds capability-gated native append support to the built-in `write` tool for #40001.

- `append: true` is opt-in and appears only when the active backend supports it.
- Docker-style and remote-shell sandboxes use a pinned `O_APPEND` mutation rather than read-modify-write.
- OpenShell remains unsupported because its mirror-sync architecture cannot provide authoritative-target append semantics.
- Unacknowledged append outcomes are fail-closed and explicitly must not be retried automatically.
- The optional Plugin SDK bridge capability and baseline are updated.

## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent writers could lose data when append was emulated by reading the whole file and overwriting it with old content plus a suffix. This change gives supported sandbox backends a native append path so independent writers do not overwrite already-persisted content.

## Lineage

This is a fresh current-main successor to closed PRs #77127 and #102243. The latter was closed after review identified that a safe sandbox implementation required a native `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` primitive; this candidate implements that boundary instead of preserving the sandbox read-modify-write path. A fresh issue/title/head search found no open append candidate for #40001.

## Evidence

**Real setup tested**

An isolated Docker container with networking disabled and a bind-mounted temporary workspace, exercised through the actual `SandboxFsBridge` and `docker exec` transport. No live gateway or production state was used.

**Current-head validation**

- Final candidate head: `056f4763ab9becd41f1ed0afe86389c76fa1bf84`, rebased onto `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`.
- All 10 changed test files passed: 153 tests across the agent and OpenShell Vitest shards.
- Core and extension source/test type gates passed on the final head.
- Plugin SDK API baseline and public surface checks passed; public wildcard reexports remained at 209.
- Full scripts lint, Control UI i18n, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The isolated Docker proof passed binary append, create-on-missing, two concurrent 128 KiB writers, restrictive `0600` creation mode, and read-only bind rejection without mutation. The append runtime blobs were verified unchanged by the subsequent base-only rebases.

**Observed result**

Supported sandbox backends append at EOF without a userspace read-modify-write cycle, and both independent writer payloads survived in the tested local-filesystem path.

**What was not tested**

- Network-filesystem append guarantees were not claimed or tested.
- OpenShell append remains intentionally unsupported.
- Append is not claimed to provide a transactional record boundary after a kernel short write.
- No idempotency key is provided; uncertain outcomes must not be automatically retried.

## Safety details

The pinned helper uses anchored directory traversal, `O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, pre/post-open regular-file checks, hardlink rejection, full first write with EINTR/short-write completion, and file/parent fsync. Append bypasses overwrite prechecks and uses backend acknowledgement as the only success signal.

Addresses #40001.

target.title: Prevent repeated byte-triggered compactions
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent repeated byte-triggered preflight compactions for the same active transcript when a previous byte-triggered compaction did not materially reduce the transcript below the configured threshold
- record byte-triggered compaction retry state on `SessionEntry` so retries require the same threshold, the same active session file, and material new growth
- preserve token-triggered preflight compaction behavior, including token compaction taking precedence when the byte retry is suppressed

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured, a byte-triggered preflight compaction can legitimately leave the active successor transcript above the threshold (for example when transcript rotation preserves branch/state history). Without retry hysteresis, the next turn can immediately trigger another byte-based preflight compaction, producing a repeated compaction loop.

This patch records the post-compaction active transcript size/file/threshold for byte-triggered compactions and suppresses another byte-triggered retry for that same active transcript until it grows materially. A retry is allowed when the active file changes, the threshold changes, or the transcript grows by at least `max(1 MiB, 10%)` from the previously recorded byte size.

Token-triggered compaction remains unchanged.

## Related

Adjacent to #88188 because both involve `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` behavior, but this PR handles the opposite failure mode: byte-triggered preflight compaction firing repeatedly after a prior byte-triggered compaction leaves the active transcript above threshold.

## Real setup tested

Staged runtime validation in a clean upstream checkout on the current branch. The proof harness used a temporary session store/transcript file, called the real `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` runtime path, and replaced only the compaction executor with a recording stub so the trigger/skip decision still came from the production preflight guard. No production runtime or private deployment state was used for PR validation.

## Exact steps or command run after this patch

From the repository checkout:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts

git diff --check

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p tsconfig.core.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-byteguard.tsbuildinfo
```

## Evidence

- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`: 53 tests passed
- `session-updates.test.ts` + `session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts`: 5 tests passed
- `tsgo` core project check passed
- formatting check passed
- diff whitespace check passed

New coverage includes:

- first byte-threshold crossing still triggers preflight compaction
- same active transcript + same threshold + no material growth suppresses repeated byte-triggered compaction
- changed active session file does not suppress retry
- changed threshold does not suppress retry
- material transcript growth allows retry
- token-triggered compaction still runs when byte retry is suppressed
- rotated successor file and byte size are recorded after byte-triggered compaction
- byte-triggered metadata is persisted through `incrementCompactionCount`
- ordinary token compactions do not write byte-triggered retry metadata

## Observed result after fix

The repeated byte-trigger retry condition is blocked for the same active transcript until there is material new growth, while token-triggered compaction and legitimate byte retries remain available.

Additional staged runtime proof from `tmp/pr-95885-proof/run-preflight-compaction-proof.ts` on head `bba688c7bc9de4aa9d511591a4b1a77b7ddacb34`:

```json
{"step":"byte-trigger first preflight","compactCallsBefore":0,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"transcript_bytes","currentTokenCount":124,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"byte-trigger same transcript retry","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":false,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"token-trigger still compacts","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":2,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"tokens","currentTokenCount":902,"sessionId":"token-session","compactionCount":1}
{"proof":"summary","totalCompactCalls":2,"triggers":["transcript_bytes","tokens"]}
```

This covers the runtime behavior ClawSweeper requested: the first byte-threshold crossing still compacts, the same active transcript/threshold retry is suppressed when there is no material growth, and token-triggered compaction still runs.


## What was not tested

- No production runtime or private deployment state was used.
- This PR does not change successor transcript pruning semantics; it only prevents immediate retry loops when a byte-triggered compaction does not materially shrink the active transcript.
- End-to-end UI notification behavior is not changed or tested here.

## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 6:58 AM (US Eastern Time) / 10:58 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 17, 2026, 6:57 AM (US Eastern Time) / 10:57 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
