target.title: fix(github-copilot): redact credential-shaped text in embedding API errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub Copilot embeddings integration echoes credential-shaped text into user-visible error diagnostics. Both non-2xx paths — model discovery (`discoverEmbeddingModels`) and the embeddings call itself (`createGitHubCopilotEmbeddingProvider`) — send a Copilot bearer token to a configurable base URL, then interpolate the bounded upstream response body verbatim into the thrown `Error`. If an upstream or proxy response reflected token-shaped or credential-shaped data, that content surfaced unredacted in error messages, logs, and any operator-facing diagnostics for the Copilot embeddings provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both error paths now wrap the bounded response body read with `redactSensitiveText(..., { mode: "tools" })` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` before interpolation.

The explicit `{ mode: "tools" }` is the important part: these errors are a credential-safety boundary, so masking must not inherit the operator's general logging preference. Called without options, `redactSensitiveText` resolves `logging.redactSensitive` and returns the input unchanged when that setting is `off` (see `src/logging/redact.ts`), which would defeat the fix. Forcing `tools` mode keeps the reflected body masked regardless of that setting.

This reuses the established in-boundary SDK redaction helper (already used elsewhere in the tree) and the existing `readResponseTextLimited` reader, so no new dependency, abstraction, or boundary crossing is introduced. The existing 8 KiB streaming read bound (`COPILOT_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`) is preserved, and the exact error message prefixes are unchanged (`GitHub Copilot model discovery HTTP <status>:` and `GitHub Copilot embeddings HTTP <status>:`). Preserving those prefixes matters because `isCopilotSetupError` matches on them for auto-selection fallback. Only the interpolated body segment is redacted; status codes and safe reason text are retained.

This addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Force redaction independently of logging settings" and its recommended maintainer option "Force boundary redaction before merge".

## User Impact

- Before: with a reflected credential in an upstream/proxy body, a Copilot embeddings failure could surface the raw token in the thrown error and logs. With `logging.redactSensitive: off`, even the prior redaction attempt would have passed the raw body through unchanged.
- After: the reflected body segment is masked at both error boundaries regardless of `logging.redactSensitive`, while the HTTP status and human-readable failure reason are preserved. No change to success paths, error message prefixes, Copilot setup detection, or auto-selection fallback.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 2 files.
- `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.ts` (+16/-2): force-redaction at both non-2xx error boundaries.
- `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` (+238, new): real-transport regression proof.

### Regression test

`extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` drives the production adapter (`githubCopilotMemoryEmbeddingProviderAdapter`) against a loopback `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0`. It does **not** mock `fetch`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime`, or `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` (`redactSensitiveText` is exercised end to end). Only auth/token resolution uses synthetic fixtures. Four cases:

1. **Model discovery error (401)** — server body contains `ghu_...`; asserts the thrown error keeps `HTTP 401` and `authentication failed` but does NOT contain the full token or its `UNIQUESECRET` component.
2. **Embeddings error (429)** — server body contains `gho_...`; asserts `HTTP 429` and `rate limit exceeded` preserved, token and `UNIQUEEMBSECRET` component absent.
3. **Redaction disabled in config (403)** — writes an on-disk config with `logging.redactSensitive: "off"` (via `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), then asserts the `ghu_...` token is still masked. This is the guard for the forced-`tools`-mode boundary: a config-honoring call would leak the token here.
4. **Success path (200)** — asserts a valid embeddings response still returns a numeric vector of the expected length, proving no behavior change on the happy path.

### Pre-submit checks: ✅ PASSED on Linux

All checks validated on Linux checkout:

target.title: fix(auto-reply): bound AGENTS.md read in post-compaction context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readPostCompactionContext` reads a workspace's `AGENTS.md` to extract a small (<=1800 char) section for the post-compaction continuation prompt, but it read the entire file with an unbounded `fs.readFileSync(opened.fd, "utf-8")` first. A pathologically large `AGENTS.md` forced an unbounded memory allocation at compaction time - exactly when memory is already under pressure.

This mirrors the bound-reads hardening applied to hook metadata in #101472 (`readFileDescriptorBoundedSync`) and the federated certificate read in #109864: workspace metadata reads should be bounded so a misconfigured or oversized file cannot trigger an unbounded read. The sibling site `compaction-safeguard.ts:1017` (`readWorkspaceContextForSummary`) reads `AGENTS.md` the same way and is left as a follow-up.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync(opened.fd, "utf-8")` with `readFileDescriptorBoundedSync(opened.fd, POST_COMPACTION_AGENTS_MD_MAX_BYTES).toString("utf-8")` - the same shared helper adopted by #101472 (`src/infra/file-descriptor-read.ts`) - with a 2 MiB limit aligned to the existing `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` (2 MiB) used for other workspace reads.
- On overflow the function catches `RangeError`, emits a `post-compaction-context` subsystem warning naming the path and limit, and returns `null` (graceful skip - consistent with the existing null-on-no-sections / null-on-no-file behavior; downstream callers already handle `null`).
- Added two tests in `post-compaction-context.test.ts`:
  - `returns null when AGENTS.md exceeds the byte read limit` - a >2 MiB `AGENTS.md` that contains a valid `## Session Startup` section returns `null`. An unbounded read would have extracted the section header and returned non-null, so this asserts the bound actually triggers.
  - `extracts sections from an AGENTS.md just under the byte read limit` - a file 1 byte under the limit still extracts its section, proving the bound is not too aggressive for legitimate files.
- Local prechecks green: `vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/post-compaction-context.test.ts` -> 27 passed, 2 skipped; `oxlint` clean; `tsgo:core:test` exit 0.

target.title: fix(gateway): config hot-reload permanently disables after sporadic recovered watcher errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running a long-lived gateway would silently lose config hot-reload: after a handful of transient file-watcher errors spread over the process lifetime, edits to `openclaw.json` stop being picked up until the gateway is restarted, even though every watcher recovery in between succeeded and served reloads normally.

The watcher re-create retry budget (3 attempts native, then degrade to polling, then 3 attempts polling, then `hot-reload disabled`) is consumed cumulatively across the whole process lifetime. A gateway that hits one recoverable inotify/kqueue error every few days — each followed by days of healthy watching — still marches irreversibly toward polling degradation and then permanent disable, because nothing ever refills the budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watcher events (`add`/`change`/`unlink`) now route through a small wrapper that resets the re-create retry counter before scheduling the shared refresh path. A delivered file event is proof the recovered watcher works, so the bounded budget applies per failure episode instead of per process lifetime. Consecutive errors with no event in between still consume the same bounded budget, so genuinely persistent failures (e.g. exhausted inotify watches) degrade and disable exactly as before.

The reset intentionally hangs off the watcher event path only: `notifyPluginMetadataChanged` (added on current `main`) also calls the shared `scheduleExternalRefresh`, and a plugin-metadata refresh proves nothing about watcher health, so it does not touch the budget. The branch is rebased onto current `main` with that newer lifecycle behavior preserved.

## User Impact

Config hot-reload on long-lived gateways now survives sporadic recoverable watcher errors indefinitely. Persistent watcher failures behave exactly as before: bounded native retries, polling fallback, then a logged `config hot-reload disabled` with `hotReloadStatus()` reporting `disabled`.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real chokidar watcher, real file, real timers)

Driver: the production `startGatewayConfigReloader` watching a real temp `openclaw.json` with a real chokidar FSWatcher in native (non-polling) mode and real backoff timers. Each round performs a real `fs.writeFile` config edit (delivered by the real watcher and consumed by the reloader), then injects one transient error on the live FSWatcher instance — the same `error`-event path a kernel-level failure takes. Four rounds, one more than the retry budget.

Before (current `main`): the budget never refills, so recovered episodes still march toward degradation — the attempt counter climbs every round and round 4 exhausts native mode:

```
[proof] real watcher delivered a file event (#1)
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #1)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #1
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #2)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 2/3 in 2000ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #2
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #3)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 3/3 in 5000ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #3
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #4)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher native retries exhausted; degrading to polling mode: Error: simulated transient watcher failure #4
```

Four more sporadic-but-recovered errors in polling mode reach `config hot-reload disabled` permanently.

After (this patch): every recovered episode refills the budget — each error is `attempt 1/3`, the watcher stays in native mode, and hot reload stays active:

```
[proof] real watcher delivered a file event (#1)
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #1)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #1
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #2)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #2
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #3)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #3
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #4)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #4
[proof] round 4: hotReloadStatus=active watchersCreated=5
[proof] FINAL hotReloadStatus=active after 4 recovered errors
[proof] file events delivered=4, reload commits=4
```

### Regression coverage

- New test in `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` (`keeps hot-reload active when transient errors are separated by working watchers`): four error/recovery rounds, each recovered watcher proving itself with a delivered file event before the next error. Fails against unfixed `main` (fourth error degrades to polling despite every recovery working); passes with the fix.
- The pre-existing exhaustion tests (back-to-back errors with no event in between: degrade to polling, then disable) pass unchanged, proving persistent-failure behavior is preserved.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` → 134 passed on the rebased head.
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass on the two changed files.

target.title: fix(proxy): make debug CA generation recoverable
target.body:
## Summary
- Make debug proxy CA generation publish only complete key/cert pairs by writing OpenSSL output to unique temporary files before promotion.
- Serialize shared cert-dir generation with a bounded lock and reclaim abandoned lock tokens safely.
- Clean failed generation output without recursively deleting user-controlled CA output paths.

Refs #109106.

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Chore

## Scope
- [ ] Gateway
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] Auth
- [ ] Memory
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API
- [ ] UI/UX
- [ ] CI
- [x] Proxy capture

## Verification
- `env PATH=/home/0668001394/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/ca.test.ts` -> passed 1 Vitest shard.
- `env PATH=/home/0668001394/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.managed-proxy.test.ts` -> passed 2 Vitest shards, 11 tests.
- `env PATH=/home/0668001394/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin:$PATH ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/proxy-capture/ca.ts src/proxy-capture/ca.test.ts` -> all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check` -> passed.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A stale partial `root-ca.pem` no longer gets reused, and a successful debug proxy CA generation leaves only a complete reusable `root-ca.pem` / `root-ca-key.pem` pair.

**Environment tested:** Linux workspace, Node 24.16.0, OpenSSL resolved through the production `ensureDebugProxyCa` path.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual patched `ensureDebugProxyCa` source via `node --import tsx`, starting with a temp cert directory that contained only a stale partial `root-ca.pem`, then called it again to verify reuse.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
{
  "before": [
    "root-ca.pem"
  ],
  "caPair": {
    "certBasename": "root-ca.pem",
    "keyBasename": "root-ca-key.pem",
    "elapsedMs": 205,
    "subject": "CN=OpenClaw Debug Proxy",
    "validTo": "Jul 24 10:54:52 2026 GMT",
    "keyType": "rsa"
  },
  "after": [
    "root-ca-key.pem",
    "root-ca.pem"
  ],
  "tempOrLockFilesAfterGeneration": [],
  "reusedSamePaths": true,
  "afterReuse": [
    "root-ca-key.pem",
    "root-ca.pem"
  ]
}
```

**Observed result:** The production function replaced the partial cert-only state with a valid RSA key/cert pair, left no temporary or lock files behind, and reused the same paths on the next call.

**Not tested:** A live macOS System Keychain trust operation from `scripts/proxy-install-ca.mjs`; the CA generation path it calls was exercised directly.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: OpenSSL wrote key and certificate outputs directly to the reusable paths, so a timeout or killed child could leave one canonical file behind.
- Missing guardrail: There was no generation lock, no temporary promotion boundary, and no regression coverage for partial output retry.

## Regression Test Plan
- Added `src/proxy-capture/ca.test.ts` for reuse, temp-file promotion, retry after failed generation, abandoned lock recovery, active lock waiting, non-recursive cleanup, and same-directory concurrent calls.
- The focused test is the smallest reliable guardrail because `ensureDebugProxyCa` is the shared production entry point used by the proxy CLI, proxy server, and CA installer.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes
Debug proxy startup and CA installation can recover from interrupted CA generation instead of reusing incomplete CA files or requiring manual cleanup of partial outputs.

## Security Impact
- New permissions? No.
- Secrets handling changed? No.
- New network calls? No.
- CA output cleanup now avoids recursively deleting directories at user-configurable output paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where native MCP OAuth credentials and authorization state used a separate JSON-plus-file-lock store. That storage model sat outside OpenClaw's canonical state database and made refresh, logout, migration, and cross-process conflict handling depend on filesystem behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

MCP OAuth now uses the shared SQLite state database as its only runtime store. Login, refresh, logout, resource challenges, and terminal token rejection run under a shared SQLite lease; the HTTP transport keeps authorization retries inside that fenced owner. `openclaw doctor --fix` is the sole legacy migration owner: it imports exact validated JSON under exclusive state ownership, records a receipt, verifies cleanup, and never creates a runtime fallback.

The migration intentionally does not dual-read or dual-write. Malformed, ambiguous, changing, or contended legacy state remains in place with actionable Doctor output. A replacement token rejected by the resource is marked for explicit reauthorization, preventing refresh loops across later requests.

AI-assisted implementation. I reviewed the storage, migration, OAuth, MCP SDK, and Codex projection paths and understand the resulting ownership model.

## User Impact

New MCP OAuth sessions persist only in `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Existing installations with files under `state/mcp-oauth` must run `openclaw doctor --fix`; valid credentials are imported and the retired JSON is removed only after verification. Corrupt or actively owned files fail closed.

Operators gain serialized cross-process refresh and logout behavior, request cancellation during OAuth work, preserved challenge metadata, and a clear explicit-login path when refreshed credentials are rejected.

Release note: MCP OAuth credentials and refresh state now persist in SQLite. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` once to import legacy MCP OAuth JSON.

## Evidence

- 86 focused state-lease, OAuth resolver, bearer retry, transport, and Doctor migration tests passed across four Vitest shards.
- Exact-head fixup proof passed 53 provider, refresh, lease, Doctor import, and stale-lock tests.
- Exact-head reauthorization-status proof passed 47 MCP OAuth and CLI tests; status and Doctor now surface terminal authorization-required state even when recoverable tokens remain stored.
- Exact-head separate-process CLI proof confirmed retained tokens report `authorization-required`, Doctor emits the explicit-login warning, and no retired OAuth file or lock store is created: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109844#issuecomment-5002567430
- Blacksmith Testbox changed gates passed formatting, generated baselines, core and test typechecks, full core lint, Kysely/database-first guards, SDK boundaries, import cycles, and architecture checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29567071520 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29569505295
- Hosted-parity Knip and Madge proof passed with zero unused exports and zero cycles: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29570823412
- Real separate-process OAuth and Doctor migration proof passed fresh PKCE login, strict resource validation, rejected-access refresh with body replay, terminal rejection, reauthorization recovery, legacy import and cleanup, logout tombstoning, and no retired file emission: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109844#issuecomment-5001825033
- Final structured autoreviews found no accepted or actionable findings. Independent exact-tree audit passed.
- Current-main integration passed the 49-test Google Meet suite, extension boundary guard, docs-map generator/check, targeted formatting, and `git diff --check`.
- Source-blind CLI smoke emitted only the normal shared SQLite bootstrap state and no retired OAuth JSON, JSONL, TXT, or lock sidecar.
- MCP SDK 1.29.0 source was checked for authorization, discovery, and transport retry behavior.
- Codex source at `35b33e4304a262965d3816da36d4991802fd5269` was checked for MCP bearer projection and refresh behavior; Codex continues to receive the same bearer-only configuration and no refresh token.

target.title: fix(onboard): keep configured AI route when guarded setup is skipped
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rerunning guarded onboarding with an already configured AI route would be told to add AI later, and would never reach the hatch TUI, when they declined machine discovery and either skipped replacement setup or had no replacement choices. The manual stage returned `null` for both "keep the current route" and "continue without AI", and the caller treated both states as cancellation (`src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:596`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`listManualSetupInferenceOptions()` already owns the config-only classification and reports `setupComplete` when a default model is configured. The guided onboarding caller now carries that fact into the manual stage, preserves the existing route for both skip paths, and continues through the normal configured-install hatch handoff without rendering an empty applied summary.

## User Impact

Guarded users can decline discovery without losing the onboarding handoff for an AI route that is already configured. Fresh installs with no active route keep the existing cancellation and "add AI later" behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Guarded onboarding preserves an already configured inference route when discovery is declined and no replacement route is selected or available.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, commit `f3fd29b47e43` on branch `fix/guarded-onboarding-keep-configured-route`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-guarded-route.mts` - writes an isolated configured-model state, executes the real guided onboarding entry point with guarded/manual selections and zero replacement choices, and records the hatch handoff.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  PASS selections=guarded,manual keptRoute=true hatch=true
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The current route is retained, setup application is not invoked, and onboarding hands the configured workspace to the hatch TUI.
- **What was not tested:** A real provider turn and interactive terminal rendering were not exercised because the failure occurs before provider activation; the runtime proof uses the production onboarding flow with deterministic prompt and handoff adapters.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/onboard-guided.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       30 passed (30)

$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

The regression test failed before the source fix because `launchHatchTui` had zero calls. Coverage now includes both an explicit replacement skip and a configured route with zero manual/auth choices.

Structured Codex autoreview was attempted with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`, but the review transport returned HTTP 403 before a model response. The changed function, caller, config-only `setupComplete` producer, sibling active-route path, and adjacent tests were reviewed manually.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - configured guarded reruns now continue to the hatch instead of exiting as AI-less.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config shape, default, persistence, or migration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - the patch only changes control flow after config-only route classification.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - no provider activation contract or plugin surface changes.
- Highest-risk area: Distinguishing a deliberate AI-less skip from retaining a previously configured route.
- Mitigation: The existing `setupComplete` contract is used as the discriminator, with separate regressions for skip and empty-choice paths plus a direct runtime proof.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: perf(ci): stabilize dependency snapshot refresh
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Blacksmith sticky disks reached the 1,000-entry installation limit, causing cache mounts to return 429 and CI shards to fall back to cold work. PR #109929 landed the overlapping Vitest and Gradle O(1) key repair while this PR was under review. This follow-up closes the remaining dependency-snapshot lifecycle gaps.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dependency v3 key stays stable: one disk per supported Node line, with no new key version or migration allocation. Snapshot validity now uses the runner OS, architecture, exact resolved Node version, and install-input hash, so a Node patch or platform mismatch cannot false-hit the warm tree.

Required CI jobs and pull requests only clone the dependency snapshot. The non-cancelled cache-warmer workflow is the sole writer. A successful `main` push CI run triggers a dependency-only refresh; scheduled and repository-dispatch runs remain the deadline fallback and also warm Vitest and compile caches. Noncanonical planner-selected Node versions keep coverage through Actions cache instead of allocating writerless sticky disks.

The repository-wide guard now rejects PR, commit, branch, run, and dependency-hash dimensions in every pinned Blacksmith sticky key.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. CI gets bounded disk cardinality, exact dependency-tree validation, and one serialized snapshot writer without coupling required builds to a cancel-on-pending cache mutex.

## Evidence

- Live pre-fix evidence: run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29570977025 mounted the dependency v3 key but received `current_count: 1000`, `limit: 1000`, then installed cold.
- Focused guard suite at rebased head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 80 passed, 1 skipped.
- Workflow sanity: `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` — actionlint, zizmor, and composite interpolation guard passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox changed gate before the overlap rebase: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29574187725 — passed in 2m36s command time.
- Fresh post-rebase autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.88.

Operational follow-up after merge: remove obsolete Blacksmith entries by legacy prefix in the Sticky Disks dashboard, then dispatch the warmer. The official deletion action accepts exact keys only, so a committed wildcard cleanup workflow cannot safely remove historical PR/hash entries.

No changelog entry: CI-only maintenance.

target.title: fix(agents): add timeout to fd and ripgrep search executions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `find` and `grep` agent session tools spawn their helper binaries (`fd` /
`rg`) via `spawnCommand(...)` with only `buffer: false, reject: false, stdio`
options — no execution timeout. If the helper stalls on a broken filesystem or
dead network mount (spawns fine, emits nothing, never exits), the tool call
hangs indefinitely and only settles when the outer abort fires — and the abort
signal is optional, so callers without one hang forever.

Merged #109215 fixed the same hang class for the `ensureTool` **availability
checks** in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts` (verified: its diff touches only
`tools-manager.ts` + its test). It deliberately did **not** touch the search
**execution** path — `find.ts` and `grep.ts` still spawn `fd`/`rg` with no
timeout. This PR closes that remaining gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each tool arms a bounded 60s execution timer (`FD_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` /
`RG_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS`) right after spawning the helper, mirroring the manual
`setTimeout` + kill pattern the sibling `bash.ts` tool already uses for its
`timeout` option (execa's native `timeout` option does not fit here: these tools
consume the child via `close` events + readline streaming, not the buffered
result promise, and `runCommandWithTimeout` is a buffered one-shot runner).

On expiry the timer kills the child through the existing `stopChild()` path
(the same kill used for abort and match-limit stops) and rejects with a clean
error in the local message style: `fd timed out after 60 seconds` /
`ripgrep timed out after 60 seconds`. Settlement stays one-shot through the
existing `settle()` guard, so the timeout **composes** with the tool-call abort
signal instead of replacing it — whichever fires first wins, and settlement
disarms the other (`clearTimeout` in `settle`/`cleanup` next to the existing
`removeEventListener`). Streaming behavior (`buffer: false` + readline) is
unchanged, and the timer is always cleared on settlement so normal searches
never retain the event loop.

No new config, env var, or tool option: the constant is consistent with
sibling bounds in `tools-manager.ts` (`ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`).

## User Impact

- `find`/`grep` tool calls can no longer hang forever on a stalled `fd`/`rg`
  child (broken mounts, wedged filesystems); they fail cleanly after 60s with
  an actionable error, even when the caller passes no abort signal.
- Normal searches are unaffected: the timer only fires if the child has not
  exited within 60s, and is cleared on every settlement path.

## Evidence

### Mechanism — timeout composes with the existing abort wiring

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outer abort (existing, optional) | `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` | 187 | `signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true })` |
| Execution bound (new) | `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` | 54 | `FD_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` |
| Timer armed at spawn | `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` | 299 | `setTimeout` → `stopChild?.()` + one-shot `settle(reject)` |
| Disarm on settlement | `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` | 188 | `clearTimeout(execTimeout)` inside `settle()` |
| Outer abort (existing, optional) | `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` | 191 | `signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true })` |
| Execution bound (new) | `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` | 54 | `RG_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` |
| Timer armed at spawn | `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` | 279 | `setTimeout` → one-shot `settle(reject)` → `stopChild()` |
| Disarm on settlement | `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts` | 172 | `clearTimeout(execTimeout)` inside `cleanup()` |

### Real behavior proof — stalled helpers through the production entry point

Standalone proof script (not committed; zero `vi.mock`). It places stub `fd`/`rg`
binaries in `$OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR/bin` that spawn successfully, emit nothing, and
never exit — the observable shape of a helper stalled on a broken filesystem or
dead network mount. `ensureTool` resolves the stubs first
(`tools-manager.ts:128-132` checks the managed bin dir before PATH), and the
script calls the real `createFindToolDefinition().execute(...)` /
`createGrepToolDefinition().execute(...)` with no abort signal, racing each
against a 70s watchdog.

Before fix (unmodified `main` @ `19b5e564d7`) — both calls hang past the 60s
bound:

```json
{
  "expectedBoundMs": 60000,
  "watchdogMs": 70000,
  "results": [
    { "tool": "find", "outcome": "pending", "elapsedMs": 70036 },
    { "tool": "grep", "outcome": "pending", "elapsedMs": 70035 }
  ]
}
```

After fix (this PR) — both calls reject at ~60s with the new clean errors:

```json
{
  "expectedBoundMs": 60000,
  "watchdogMs": 70000,
  "results": [
    { "tool": "find", "outcome": "rejected", "message": "fd timed out after 60 seconds", "elapsedMs": 60114 },
    { "tool": "grep", "outcome": "rejected", "message": "ripgrep timed out after 60 seconds", "elapsedMs": 60139 }
  ]
}
```

### Control-red

The "before" run above **is** the control-red: the identical script on
unmodified `main` leaves both tool calls pending at the 70s watchdog (10s past
the fix's 60s bound). Reverting this PR is deleting the two `setTimeout` blocks
(plus the constants and `clearTimeout` lines) — the diff in this PR is purely
additive, so the before/after pair exercises exactly the added lines.

### Regression tests

Two new tests per tool in `find.fd.test.ts` / `grep.stream-errors.test.ts`
(mirroring the existing mocked-child style): a hanging child that never emits
output and never closes now rejects with `fd timed out after 60 seconds` /
`ripgrep timed out after 60 seconds` and kills the child; a normally-exiting
child leaves zero pending timers (`vi.getTimerCount() === 0`) and is never
killed. Existing abort-precedence tests (`settles an abort when the spawned
child never closes`, etc.) still pass unchanged, confirming the timeout does
not alter abort semantics.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/find.fd.test.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/tools/find.test.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/tools/find.fd.test.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.stream-errors.test.ts
✓ clean (0 errors)
```

### tsgo

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json
→ no errors in any file touched by this PR
```

(Local worktree note: the full-project runs report 3 pre-existing
`packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors caused by a stale shared
`node_modules` predating the latest `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `main`; that file is
untouched by this PR and the same command passes on a deps-matched checkout.
The oxlint wrapper's extension-boundary dts pre-step was skipped with the
sanctioned `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1` for the same reason — this PR does
not touch `extensions/` or `packages/`.)

### git diff --check

clean — 4 files, +103/-0 (2 source files, 2 test files).


---

## Round 2 (2026-07-17)

**Review addressed:** P1 on `find.ts:299` (same class in `grep.ts`) — the 60s deadline only called the existing stop path, but a wedged fd/rg can ignore the default termination signal, leaving the process and its pipes alive after the tool promise rejects. The reviewer asked for definitive termination or bounded escalation in both tools, a test with a child that ignores the initial signal, and stream cleanup after forced settlement.

**Repair (both `find.ts` and `grep.ts`):**

- The fd/rg children are now spawned with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (the repo's established 300ms kill-grace constant from `src/process/exec-spawn.ts`, the same escalation `runExec` and `exec-termination.ts` already use). execa monkey-patches `subprocess.kill()`, so the existing stop path still sends SIGTERM first, then automatically escalates to SIGKILL if the child has not exited within the grace window. This covers the 60s deadline path, the match-limit stop, and the outer-abort stop uniformly — no new kill machinery.
- On deadline settlement the tool now also closes the readline interface and destroys `stdout`/`stderr`, so even a child stuck in uninterruptible sleep cannot pin stream handles past settlement ("stream cleanup after forced settlement").
- The 60s value and the wall-clock semantics are unchanged (maintainer decision on inactivity-vs-wall-clock is pending and orthogonal). The only new seam is an optional `execTimeoutMs` on `FindToolOptions`/`GrepToolOptions` (documented as a test seam, resolved via the shared `resolveTimerTimeoutMs`) so the escalation can be exercised without a 60s wait; production callers keep the default.

**Regression coverage (new `find.exec-timeout.test.ts` / `grep.exec-timeout.test.ts`, POSIX-gated):** each test writes a real managed-bin stub (node shebang script that swallows SIGTERM) to a temp dir, points `ensureTool` at it, and runs the real `spawnCommand` (spied via an `importActual` passthrough) with `execTimeoutMs: 100`. Assertions: the tool call rejects with the timeout error; the child's stdio streams are destroyed at settlement; and the process is actually reaped afterwards (`process.kill(pid, 0)` → ESRCH within a 5s poll — only possible via the SIGKILL escalation, since the stub ignores SIGTERM). An `afterEach` SIGKILLs any surviving stub so a failing run cannot hang the worker.

**Control-red proof:** with the escalation stripped (no `forceKillAfterDelay`, no stream destroy, timeout seam kept), both new tests fail — `AssertionError: expected false to be true` on the stream-cleanup assertion, and the wedged stub survives (reaped by the test's `afterEach` safety net). With the escalation restored, all four find/grep test files pass: 19/19 (including the round-1 fake-timer timeout tests and `find.test.ts` on the unit-fast lane).

**Checks (round 2):**

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts` on the four find/grep test files — 19/19 passed; `find.test.ts` on `vitest.unit-fast.config.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0; `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — exit 0
- `oxlint` on the four changed/new files — clean; `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and any-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that (1) heading checks block valid headingless skills, (2) any-line overlap is trivially bypassable — a plan document sharing a single heading or boilerplate line receives `requiresExplicitApproval=false` and overwrites the skill, and (3) zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser, rejects empty bodies, and uses a **substantial-continuity classifier** that requires at least 3 shared non-heading body lines AND at least 50% of original non-heading content retained before allowing automatic apply. Low-continuity updates force pending approval even under `auto` policy, preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites while blocking incidental-overlap plans that share only headings or 1-2 boilerplate lines.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Low-continuity update proposals (insufficient shared content with current SKILL.md) are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid headingless skill updates apply normally when they retain substantial content
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`**

**Live approval-hook proof (terminal transcript from exact head)**:

The `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` function is the approval hook that determines whether an agent-initiated `apply` action proceeds automatically or requires operator approval. Under `auto` policy, it returns `undefined` (no approval required) for actions that pass all checks. For low-continuity updates, it returns `requireApproval` with a warning prompt, which blocks the agent from applying the proposal until the operator approves. SKILL.md remains unchanged until approval is granted.

```console
=== Approval-Hook Real Behavior Proof ===
SHA: e0dc28d1ea33
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T10:15:40.062Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Low-continuity update blocked by approval hook (auto policy) ---
SKILL.md before proposal:
  ---
  name: weather
  description: Weather skill
  ---
  
  # Weather
  
  Steps to check weather.
  Check the forecast.
  Save the result.

Approval hook result: requireApproval (BLOCKED)
  title: "Apply workspace skill proposal"
  severity: "warning"
  allowedDecisions: ["allow-once","deny"]
SKILL.md unchanged after approval hook block: true

--- Proof 2: Incidental heading-only overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 3: Incidental 1-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 4: Incidental 2-line overlap blocked ---
applySkillProposal result.requiresExplicitApproval: true

--- Proof 5: Substantial continuity update allowed (auto policy) ---
Approval hook result: undefined (ALLOWED)

--- Proof 6: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged after rejection: true

=== Summary ===
1. Low-continuity update: approval hook returns requireApproval, SKILL.md unchanged ✅
2. Heading-only overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
3. 1-line overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
4. 2-line overlap: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
5. Substantial continuity: approval hook returns undefined (allowed) ✅
6. Empty body: hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged ✅
```

**Substantial-continuity classifier detail** (exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`):

```console
Original SKILL.md body (non-heading lines):
  "Steps to check weather.", "Check the forecast.", "Save the result." (3 lines)

Heading-only overlap (shares "# Weather" heading, no non-heading overlap):
  overlapCount=0, ratio=0.0 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

1-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather.", 1/3=33%):
  overlapCount=1, ratio=0.33 → 1<3 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

2-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather." + "Check the forecast.", 2/3=67%):
  overlapCount=2, ratio=0.67 → 2<3 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

Substantial continuity (shares 4/6 non-heading lines, 67%):
  overlapCount=4, ratio=0.67 → 4≥3 && 0.67≥0.5 → isSubstantialContinuity=true
  → requiresExplicitApproval=false, auto-apply proceeds ✅
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA `e0dc28d1ea33`)**:

target.title: fix(ci): bound CLI installer smoke curl with connect and max-time
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root CLI installer smoke (`scripts/test-install-sh-docker.sh`) pipes `curl` directly into `bash` inside the non-root container with no curl-level timeout:

```bash
"$NONROOT_IMAGE" -lc "curl -fsSL \"$CLI_INSTALL_URL\" | bash -s -- --set-npm-prefix --no-onboard"
```

`curl` has no default connect or total timeout, so a stalled CDN connect or hung response body pins the container until the outer `INSTALL_SMOKE_DOCKER_RUN_TIMEOUT` docker-run budget kills the run. The same shape was already fixed for the main installer smoke (`scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh`) and the install-sh-e2e runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh`), but the CLI installer smoke was left bare.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the curl with the same `--connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300` shape already used by the sibling install-sh-smoke and install-sh-e2e runners, and enable `pipefail` so curl download failures are not masked by the bash consumer that follows.

## User Impact

CI lane reliability. The CLI installer smoke lane can no longer be held hostage by a single hung connect or partial response body.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof captured locally (Darwin 25.5.0) against RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 address `192.0.2.1`, which is guaranteed unroutable and reproduces a stalled-connect scenario deterministically. Env proxies were unset so the curl in the test talks directly to the network stack. Each test runs the exact pipeline shape used in `scripts/test-install-sh-docker.sh` (with smaller budgets so the proof itself stays bounded).

**Test A — PR pipeline shape (`set -o pipefail` + `--connect-timeout` + `--max-time`), stalled connect exits within budget and curl failure propagates:**

```
$ time bash -lc 'set -o pipefail; curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 \
    "http://192.0.2.1/install.sh" | bash -s -- --dry-run'
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5009 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
bash -lc  0.01s user 0.01s system 0% cpu 5.023 total
pipeline exit: 28
```

**Test B — same curl invocation but WITHOUT `set -o pipefail` (the pre-PR shape): curl still times out, but the exit code is masked to 0 by the downstream bash consumer:**

```
$ time bash -lc 'curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 \
    "http://192.0.2.1/install.sh" | bash -s -- --dry-run'
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
bash -lc  0.00s user 0.01s system 0% cpu 5.025 total
pipeline exit: 0
```

**Test C — current `main` shape (bare `curl | bash`, no curl-level budget): the pipeline hangs on the stalled connect and only exits when an outer killer signal arrives (mirroring how the Docker smoke currently depends on the 2,700s outer `INSTALL_SMOKE_DOCKER_RUN_TIMEOUT` to clean up):**

```
$ bash -lc 'curl -fsSL "http://192.0.2.1/install.sh" | bash -s -- --dry-run' &
$ PID=$!; ( sleep 8 && kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null ) & wait $PID
main shape survives until outer kill (would run forever under docker); exit=137
```

**Test D — positive case: the PR pipeline shape still completes cleanly when curl succeeds, so `pipefail` does not introduce false negatives:**

```
$ bash -lc 'set -o pipefail; echo "installer body" | bash -c "cat > /dev/null; echo consumer-ran"'
consumer-ran
pipeline exit: 0
```

Summary of behavior change:

| Scenario | Pre-PR (main) | Post-PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stalled connect | hangs until outer docker run timeout kills the container (~2,700s budget burned) | curl exits 28 within `--max-time 300s`, pipeline propagates the failure |
| Curl failure propagation | exit 0 (masked by bash consumer) | exit 28 (surfaced via `pipefail`) |
| Normal successful run | exit 0 | exit 0 (unchanged) |

Additional static checks:

- `bash -n scripts/test-install-sh-docker.sh` parses cleanly before and after the change.
- Diff is a single one-line change to the docker `-lc` argument.
- Same `--connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300` shape as `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh` and `scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh`.

## What Problem This Solves

`readJsonFile` in the plugins-authoring command uses `JSON.parse` without try-catch when reading user-authored `package.json` files. A malformed or corrupted package.json file produces an unhelpful `SyntaxError` traceback instead of a user-friendly error message.

- Wraps `JSON.parse(raw)` in try-catch, throwing `Malformed JSON in <path>` on failure
- Test coverage: 18 new lines in plugins-authoring-command.test.ts verify the error message format

## Merge Risk

Low. The try-catch specifically targets the `JSON.parse` call in `readJsonFile`, preserving the existing behavior for valid JSON.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch and uses the shared `hasErrnoCode(err, "ENOENT")` helper from `src/infra/errors.ts` to detect the missing-file case. This reuses the canonical errno guard instead of duplicating the `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code` cast across three readers, keeping error classification on the shared contract. It then throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — clean
- `pnpm format:check src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

### Real CLI proof (via `pnpm openclaw`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json | ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/nonexistent/path/plan.json' | ENOENT. Re-run openclaw secrets apply --from <path> --dry-run to inspect the plan without writing.
EXIT: 1
```

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors.
Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node 22, `pnpm openclaw ...`.
What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged.

## Review Response

- Addressed ClawSweeper feedback to replace the three direct `NodeJS.ErrnoException` casts with the shared `hasErrnoCode` helper while preserving command-specific messages, original causes, and focused regression tests.
- The `check-lint` CI failure on the previous head was in an unrelated file (`scripts/release-candidate-checklist.d.mts`) caused by a transient upstream `main` lint issue; current `upstream/main` no longer reports that error.

target.title: fix(qqbot): surface terminal reply-session conflict failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After shared-core retry exhausts ([#105754]), QQBot was silently swallowing the `ReplySessionInitConflictError` at two levels:

1. **`outbound-dispatch.ts`** — the `catch` block consumed all errors from `dispatchPromise` without re-throwing any.
2. **`gateway.ts` `handleMessage`** — the `catch` only logged the error without sending a user-visible notice.

**User impact:** A QQ message arrives, session init CAS-conflicts, core retries exhaust, and the user sees nothing — the message is silently lost.

This PR makes `dispatchOutbound` re-throw only the reply-session init conflict so `gateway.ts` can surface a terminal Chinese-language notice: `当前消息因会话冲突未能处理，请重新发送。\n错误编号：XXXXXXXX`

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
Tests  55 passed (43 existing + 12 new), 0 regression
```

### New test coverage

| Test group | Cases |
|---|---|
| `dispatchOutbound session conflict` | conflict re-throw, unrelated passthrough, normal resolve, similar-worded no-match |
| `reply-session-conflict shared helpers` | real-helper import: error match, deterministic ID generation, padding |
| `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` | sends for conflict, no-op for unrelated, `terminal_notice_failed` on send failure, sanitized text (no sessionKey/internal paths), same error ID in log and user text |

### Format check

```
pnpm format:check -- extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts ...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Rebase

Rebased onto upstream/main (`d572c5cb2d`) with zero conflicts.

## What this PR does

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `reply-session-conflict.ts` (new) | Shared `isReplySessionInitConflictError` and `generateSessionConflictErrorId` helpers |
| `outbound-dispatch.ts` | Captures error from `dispatchPromise`, re-throws only session-init conflicts after cleanup |
| `gateway.ts` | `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` exports a testable function that detects the conflict, generates an 8-char hex error reference, logs full details, and sends a best-effort terminal notice |
| Test file | 12 new deterministic tests |

## What was already fixed (not duplicated here)

- **[#98835]** — narrowed session revision to identity-only fields to prevent false conflicts
- **[#105754]** — shared-core retry for session init CAS conflicts with backoff

## Why no second-channel retry

[#105754] is the shared conflict retry owner. Adding a second 250ms/1s/2.5s retry in the QQBot channel would:

- Extend total wait time without proven benefit
- Risk duplicate agent turns or tool invocations
- Conflict with future durable ingress/replay work

## Limitations (explicit)

- **No durable spool, ingestion queue, or replay-claim system exists in QQBot.** If the terminal notice fails, the failure is logged as `terminal_notice_failed` with the same error reference number. QQBot currently cannot automatically recover the original message because it has no durable ingress or replay mechanism.
- Durable ingress/replay/operation-idempotency is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Files changed

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/reply-session-conflict.ts` (new)
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts`

[#98835]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98835
[#105754]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105754

target.title: fix(reef): repeated relay reconnects no longer leave stale sockets active
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated Reef relay reconnects could retain abort listeners from earlier WebSocket generations. Local frame-processing failures could also leave an abandoned socket connected after its replacement started, causing listener warnings over time and stale socket activity during channel shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Reef inbox WebSocket generation now owns a named abort listener that is removed on its first terminal transition. Generations that fail locally are closed before replacement, while the existing reconnect, backoff, and remote-close behavior remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running Reef channels can reconnect repeatedly without accumulating shutdown listeners or retaining failed sockets. Channel abort now closes only the active WebSocket generation.

## Evidence

- RED on the pre-fix implementation: after the first WebSocket generation settled and a replacement started, the channel abort signal retained two listeners instead of the expected single active-generation listener.
- GREEN behavior: the controlled two-generation regression verifies that malformed input closes the failed generation, only the replacement remains subscribed to channel abort, and the final abort closes the replacement without closing the failed generation again.
- Refreshed at the current PR head (`544d3b9`): `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts` — 1 file and 14 tests passed.
- The current head's GitHub Actions checks are successful.

### Proof boundary and remaining action

No run against a real Reef relay was performed. The evidence above uses the production reconnect loop with controlled WebSocket generations and does not claim to prove real-relay close-event ordering. The local environment has no configured Reef channel or registered handle, so starting an isolated gateway would only prove gateway startup, not this relay lifecycle.

Clearing the current `needs proof` rating requires a redacted real-relay run demonstrating repeated reconnect generations, one active abort listener, closure of a locally failed socket, and clean shutdown of the replacement.

target.title: fix(e2e): keep telegram proof diagnostic tails Unicode safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram user Crabbox proof script (`scripts/e2e/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts`) bounds several diagnostic tails that surface in failure output, and two cut shapes corrupt multibyte content (gateway logs for a Telegram proof are emoji/CJK-dense):

1. `readLogTail` (exported, used by `waitForLog` readiness errors) reads the last N **bytes** of a log file and decodes with `toString("utf8")` from the cut offset. A window starting inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character emits U+FFFD replacement characters at the start of the tail — the same bug merged #109669 fixed in `scripts/e2e/lib/text-file-utils.mjs`.
2. The rolling output buffer (`spawnLogged`), command stdout tail (`appendCommandTextTail`), and the readiness-error tails (`waitForOutput`, `waitForLog`) cut with `String.slice(-N)`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair and leave a lone surrogate at the start of the diagnostics text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the repo's existing helpers instead of adding new logic: `decodeUtf8Tail` from `scripts/e2e/lib/text-file-utils.mjs` (#109669, now exported — the identical one-line export also lands in sibling PR #109923, so either merge order applies cleanly) for the byte window, and `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` for the UTF-16 cuts. Caps and tail sizes are unchanged; only the cut alignment changes, so failure diagnostics always start on a character boundary.

Root causes on `main`: `scripts/e2e/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts:1035` (byte decode from an unaligned window), `:585`, `:903`, `:925`, `:939`, `:1055` (UTF-16 `slice(-N)` cuts).

Related independent bug-family PRs: #109669 (merged, text-file utils), #109670 (parallels host server), #109923 (phase runner). Separate files, not stacked; any order merges cleanly.

## User Impact

Maintainers debugging Telegram proof failures get readable log tails instead of leading mojibake whenever emoji/CJK content crosses a tail cutoff.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof against the production exports on `main`:

Before (origin/main):

```
readLogTail(23): "���yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"   has U+FFFD: true
waitForLog error tail first char code: de00   tail has lone surrogate: true
```

(0xDE00 is the low surrogate half of U+1F600.)

After (this branch):

```
readLogTail(23): "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"   has U+FFFD: false
waitForLog error tail first char code: 62   tail has lone surrogate: false
```

Regression coverage (`test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts`, next to the existing tail tests):

- `readLogTail` drops a leading character split by the byte cut, and keeps the full emoji when the cut lands on the character boundary.
- `waitForLog` timeout error tail contains no lone surrogate when the last-4000-unit cut splits a pair.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts` — 32/32 pass on this branch; the 2 new tests fail on unpatched `telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts` (control-red verified by reverting the prod file to `origin/main`).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/e2e-text-file-utils.test.ts` — 3/3 pass (helper export is additive).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files — clean; `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json` — no errors in touched files (pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors come from a stale local `ipaddr.js@1.9.1`, unrelated).
- `git diff --check` — clean.
